q.s: The standard ratio of length, breadth and thickness followed in Harappan burnt bricks was:
q.x: Harappan bricks kept a 1:2:4 ratio, though house bricks (about 7.5x15x30 cm) and city-wall bricks (10x20x40 cm) differed in size.

q.s: In Mesopotamian records, the Indus region was referred to as:
q.x: Mesopotamian texts call the Indus region Meluhha; Dilmun is Bahrain and Magan is Oman.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Harappan contacts with West Asia is correct?
o: The closest external contact of the Harappans was with Egypt
Magan in Mesopotamian records refers to Bahrain
Harappan seals have been found at Susa, Ur and Nippur
Mesopotamian records call the Indus region Dilmun
q.x: Harappan seals occur at Susa, Ur and Nippur. The Indus region was Meluhha, Dilmun was Bahrain and Magan Oman; the closest contact was with Mesopotamia.

q.s: Scholars generally describe the political structure of the Harappan civilization as:
q.x: No king is known; uniformity of weights, bricks and town plans suggests a corporate authority with civic administration. A monarchy with Sabha and Samiti belongs to the Later Vedic age.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Harappan civilization is correct?
o: Uniform weights, bricks and town plans over a vast area point to a significant authority
Large temples are a common feature of Harappan cities
Royal palaces have been found at most Harappan sites
The Harappans had a hereditary monarchy with Sabha and Samiti
q.x: Uniformity over about 8 lakh sq km suggests a strong authority; no palaces, temples or known kings have been found.

q.s: The theory that the Arctic region was the original home of the Aryans was put forward by:
q.x: Tilak argued for the Arctic home in 'The Arctic Home in the Vedas'; A.C. Das proposed Sapta Sindhu.

q.s: The Atharvaveda describes the Sabha and the Samiti as the twin daughters of:
q.x: The Atharvaveda calls the Sabha and Samiti the two daughters of Prajapati.

q.s: Which of the following Vedas is NOT included in the 'Trayi'?
q.x: The Trayi is the first three Vedas; the Atharvaveda, the latest Veda, is left out.

q.s: The first human images of the Buddha were made during the rule of the:
q.x: Buddha images were first made in the Kushana period at Mathura and Gandhara; earlier Hinayana art showed him only through symbols.

q.s: Which of the following schools of art did NOT flourish during the Kushana period?
q.x: The Pala school of Bengal-Bihar belongs to the 8th-12th centuries.

q.s: The Nalanda Mahavihara was founded by the Gupta ruler:
q.x: Nalanda was founded by Kumaragupta I (c. 427 CE).

q.s: Which of the following Buddhist centres was NOT founded or patronised by the Palas?
q.x: Nalanda was founded by the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I, though the Palas later supported it.

q.s: Samudragupta's Prayag Prashasti was engraved on the pillar originally set up by:
q.x: The Allahabad-Kosam pillar is an Ashokan pillar; it later carried Samudragupta's prashasti and an inscription of Jahangir.

q.s: The Kosam pillar of Ashoka was moved to the Allahabad fort during the reign of:
q.x: It went to the Allahabad fort under Akbar; Firuz Shah Tughluq moved the Topra and Meerut pillars to Delhi.

q.s: The bilingual Greek-Aramaic edict of Ashoka was found at:
q.x: The bilingual edict is from Kandahar (Shar-i-Kuna); Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra edicts are in Kharosthi.

q.s: The Kharosthi script, used in some Ashokan edicts, was written:
q.x: Kharosthi, derived from Aramaic, was written from right to left; Brahmi was written left to right.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Mauryan coins is correct?
o: The mashaka was a gold coin
The pana (karshapana) was a silver coin
The kakani was worth four times a mashaka
The gold suvarna was in common daily use
q.x: The pana was silver; the mashaka was copper, the kakani was a quarter of a mashaka, and the suvarna was not in common use.

q.s: Kautilya's Arthashastra is often compared with which Western work?
q.x: The Arthashastra's statecraft is commonly compared with Machiavelli's The Prince.

q.s: According to Fa-hien, ordinary daily exchange in Gupta India was carried on with:
q.x: Fa-hien says common people used cowries; the Guptas issued gold dinaras in the largest numbers and very few copper coins.

q.s: The Mandsaur (Dashpur) inscription records that a Sun temple was built by a guild of:
q.x: The Mandsaur inscription (Kumaragupta I, Bandhuvarman) records silk weavers building a Sun temple; the Indore plate mentions an oil-men's guild.

q.s: The Junagadh inscription of Skandagupta records the repair of the Sudarshana lake by:
q.x: Skandagupta's governor Parnadatta repaired the Sudarshana lake; Rudradaman had repaired it earlier.

q.s: The Pushyabhuti dynasty, to which Harshavardhana belonged, had its early capital at:
q.x: Pushyabhuti founded the dynasty at Thanesar; Harsha later moved the capital to Kannauj.

q.s: Rajyavardhana, who preceded Harshavardhana on the throne, was Harsha's:
q.x: Rajyavardhana was Harsha's elder brother; Grahavarman Maukhari was his brother-in-law.

q.s: Harshavardhana's southward advance was checked on the banks of the Narmada by:
q.x: Pulakesin II stopped Harsha on the Narmada, as recorded in the Aihole inscription (634 CE).

q.s: The Aihole inscription, which records Pulakesin II's victory over Harsha, was composed by:
q.x: Ravikirti, Pulakesin II's court poet, composed the Aihole inscription of 634 CE.

q.s: Which Delhi Sultan made iqtas hereditary and revived the jagir system?
q.x: Firoz Tughlaq made iqtas hereditary and revived jagirs, which weakened the army; Alauddin had enlarged the khalisa.

q.s: Which of the following measures was NOT taken by Alauddin Khalji?
q.x: Firoz Tughlaq made iqtas hereditary; Alauddin enlarged the khalisa and controlled markets.

q.s: The Sultan who destroyed the temples of Mathura and broke the images of Nagarkot was:
q.x: Sikandar Lodi destroyed the Mathura temples and the Nagarkot images.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Delhi Sultanate is correct?
o: Temple destruction under the Sultans had only religious motives
Firoz Tughlaq sought recognition from the Abbasid Caliph in Egypt
The Abbasid Caliphate of Baghdad was still standing in Firoz Tughlaq's time
Ibrahim Lodi destroyed the temples of Mathura
q.x: Baghdad fell in 1258, so Firoz looked to the Caliph in Egypt; Sikandar Lodi destroyed the Mathura temples, and temple destruction also served political ends.

q.s: Shah Jahan shifted the Mughal capital from Agra to:
q.x: Shah Jahan built Shahjahanabad at Delhi (1638-48) and moved the capital there.

q.s: After his deposition in 1658, Shah Jahan was confined in Agra Fort and nursed by his daughter:
q.x: Jahanara stayed with Shah Jahan in Agra Fort till his death in 1666; Roshanara sided with Aurangzeb.

q.s: The Dhrupad style of music was developed under the patronage of:
o: Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior
q.x: Dhrupad was developed by Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior; khayal flourished under Muhammad Shah 'Rangeela'.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of musical form and its origin or patron is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Qawwali is the Sufi devotional form; Man Singh Tomar is linked with Dhrupad.

q.s: The Bhakti movement as an organised movement first began with the:
o: Alvars and Nayanars of the Tamil South
q.x: Bhakti began with the Alvars (Vaishnava) and Nayanars (Shaiva) of the Tamil South in the 6th-9th centuries.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT an Alvar saint?
q.x: Appar was a Nayanar (Shaiva) saint; the Alvars were Vaishnava.

q.s: Gaudiya Vaishnavism was founded by:
q.x: Chaitanya, born at Nabadwip in Bengal, founded Gaudiya Vaishnavism; Shankaradeva preached in Assam.

q.s: Which of the following Bhakti saints did NOT belong to the Saguna tradition?
q.x: Kabir worshipped a formless (Nirguna) God; Chaitanya, Tulsidas and Surdas were Saguna devotees.

q.s: In the Virashaiva tradition of Basavanna, 'Kayaka' stands for:
q.x: Kayaka is honest labour as worship; Dasoha is sharing surplus; the Ishtalinga is worn on the body for worship outside temples.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a concept of the Virashaiva movement of Basavanna?
q.x: Sama (musical gathering) is a Sufi practice; Kayaka, Dasoha and Ishtalinga are Virashaiva ideas.

q.s: The dargah of the Chishti saint Gesudaraz (Banda Nawaz) is located at:
q.x: Gesudaraz's dargah is at Gulbarga; Burhanuddin Gharib is linked with Khuldabad.

q.s: The Ameen Peer Dargah (Asthana-e-Magdoomiya) in Andhra Pradesh is located at:
q.x: The Ameen Peer Dargah is at Kadapa; the Baba Fakhruddin Dargah is at Penukonda.

q.s: The Portuguese navigator who reached Brazil in 1500 was:
q.x: Cabral reached Brazil in 1500 on his way to India.

q.s: The 'Cape of Storms', later renamed the Cape of Good Hope, was rounded in 1488 by:
q.x: Dias rounded it in 1487-88; King John II renamed it the Cape of Good Hope.

q.s: The Revolt of 1857 began on 10 May 1857 at:
q.x: The sepoys rose at Meerut on 10 May 1857 and marched to Delhi; Mangal Pandey's incident at Barrackpore was in March.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a leader of the rebels in the Revolt of 1857?
q.x: John Nicholson was a British officer who led the assault that recaptured Delhi.

q.s: The portfolio system in the Governor-General's council was introduced in 1859 by:
q.x: Canning introduced the portfolio system, later recognised by the Indian Councils Act, 1861.

q.s: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1861, an ordinance issued by the Viceroy in an emergency remained valid for:
q.x: The Viceroy could issue ordinances without the council's concurrence, valid for six months.

q.s: The French General who obtained the Northern Circars from Salabat Jang in 1753 was:
q.x: Bussy got the Northern Circars from Salabat Jang in 1753; Dupleix was recalled in 1754.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a French commander or governor in India?
q.x: Robert Clive was the English East India Company's commander, famous for the defence of Arcot (1751).

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the French settlements in India after the Treaty of Paris (1763)?
q.x: The French kept Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam and Chandernagore as unfortified trading posts; Machilipatnam was not among them.

q.s: By the Treaty of Amritsar (16 March 1846), Kashmir was sold to Gulab Singh for:
q.x: Kashmir went to Gulab Singh for Rs 75 lakh, founding the Dogra state of Jammu and Kashmir.

q.s: The Treaty of Amritsar (1809) between Ranjit Singh and the British fixed which river as the boundary?
q.x: The 1809 treaty, negotiated by Metcalfe under Minto, fixed the Sutlej as the boundary.

q.s: Who is called the 'Father of Civil Services in India'?
q.x: Cornwallis reorganised and Europeanised the civil service; he also gave the Cornwallis Code (1793).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with Lord Cornwallis?
q.x: The Subsidiary Alliance was introduced by Lord Wellesley.

q.s: The First Factory Act of 1881, which barred children below 7 years from factory work, was passed during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: The First Factory Act (1881) came under Ripon; the Second (1891), limiting women's hours, came under Lansdowne.

q.s: The three stages of colonialism in India (mercantile, free trade and finance capital) were set out by R.P. Dutt in his book:
o: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
q.x: R.P. Dutt described the stages in 'India Today'; 'Poverty and Un-British Rule' is by Dadabhai Naoroji.

q.s: In R.P. Dutt's scheme, the free trade (industrial capital) stage of colonialism covered the period:
q.x: The free trade stage ran from 1813 to 1858; the finance capital stage followed from 1858.

q.s: Which of the following commissions was NOT related to famines in British India?
q.x: The Hunter Commission (1882) dealt with education; Strachey (1880), Lyall (1898) and MacDonnell (1901) were famine commissions.

q.s: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was passed during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: Lytton passed the Act amid criticism of his handling of the 1876-77 famine and the Delhi Durbar of 1877; Ripon repealed it in 1882.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Vernacular Press Act, 1878 is correct?
o: A paper could get exemption by submitting proofs to the High Court
An aggrieved paper could appeal in a court of law
A magistrate needed prior permission of the provincial government to seize a press
It was passed amid criticism of Lytton over the 1876-77 famine and the Delhi Durbar
q.x: The Act followed criticism of Lytton's famine policy and the costly Durbar; magistrates needed no prior permission, there was no court appeal, and proofs went to a government censor.

q.s: In 'Thoughts on Linguistic States' (1955), B.R. Ambedkar suggested which city as a second capital of India?
q.x: Ambedkar proposed Hyderabad as a second capital; he accepted 'one state, one language' but not 'one language, one state'.

q.s: Siddharth College in Bombay, founded in 1946, was established by:
q.x: Ambedkar's People's Education Society founded Siddharth College in 1946.

q.s: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College at Aligarh was founded in the year:
q.x: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the MAO College in 1877; the Arya Samaj dates from 1875 and the Prarthana Samaj from 1867.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan?
q.x: Deoband (1866) was founded by Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi.

q.s: The first President of the Andhra Provincial Congress circle was:
q.x: Nyapati Subba Rao was the first President of the Andhra Congress circle formed after the Madras session of 1914.

q.s: The first Telugu woman to attend a session of the Indian National Congress was:
q.x: Ponaka Kanakamma attended the Kakinada session of 1923.

q.s: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1892, members of the legislative councils were allowed to:
o: Discuss the budget but not vote on it
q.x: The 1892 Act (Lansdowne) allowed discussion of the budget but no voting or amendment; election was only indirect.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Indian Councils Act, 1892?
o: Members could vote on the budget
q.x: Under the 1892 Act members could discuss the budget and ask questions but could not vote on it.

q.s: The Explosive Substances Act, passed to curb revolutionary activity, was enacted in:
q.x: The Explosive Substances Act and the Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act were of 1908; the Indian Press Act was of 1910.

q.s: Which of the following repressive laws was NOT passed in 1908?
q.x: The Indian Press Act was passed in 1910.

q.s: Who called Bal Gangadhar Tilak the 'Father of Indian Unrest'?
q.x: Valentine Chirol used the phrase in his book 'Indian Unrest' (1910).

q.s: Tilak's newspaper 'Kesari' was published in which language?
q.x: Kesari was in Marathi; his English paper was Mahratta.

q.s: The Naujawan Bharat Sabha was founded in March 1926 by Bhagat Singh at:
q.x: Bhagat Singh founded the Naujawan Bharat Sabha at Lahore with Sukhdev and Bhagwati Charan Vohra; the HRA had been founded at Kanpur.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Naujawan Bharat Sabha is correct?
o: Ambika Chakravarti was one of its early members
Surya Sen was one of its founders
It was founded at Kanpur in 1926
Sukhdev and Bhagwati Charan Vohra were among its co-founders
q.x: Bhagat Singh founded it at Lahore with Sukhdev and Bhagwati Charan Vohra; Surya Sen and Ambika Chakravarti belonged to the Chittagong group.

q.s: The Muslim League's 'Pirpur Report' (1938) was a complaint against:
o: The Congress ministries in the provinces
q.x: The Pirpur Report alleged ill-treatment of Muslims by the Congress ministries; the Sharif Report (1939) dealt with Bihar.

q.s: 'Muslim Sufferings under Congress Rule' (December 1939) was written by:
q.x: Fazlul Haq of Bengal wrote it, alleging 'Hindu Raj' under the Congress ministries.

q.s: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on:
q.x: The massacre came on 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi), a week after the Rowlatt hartal of 6 April.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among Gandhi's early satyagrahas in India during 1917-18?
q.x: The Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) was led by Vallabhbhai Patel.

q.s: The slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad' was coined by:
q.x: Hasrat Mohani coined it in 1921; Bhagat Singh later made it popular.

q.s: Which Khilafat leader gave up the title 'Haziq-ul-Mulk' during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
q.x: Hakim Ajmal Khan returned the title Haziq-ul-Mulk; the Ali brothers were arrested after the Karachi resolution of July 1921.

q.s: The title 'Desabhakta' was associated with:
q.x: Konda Venkatappayya was called Desabhakta; Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was given the title Desoddharaka.

q.s: The Telugu social novel 'Malapalli' was written by:
q.x: Unnava Lakshminarayana wrote Malapalli, a novel on untouchability; Naa Jeevitha Katha is Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao's autobiography.

q.s: The Rampa revolt of 1879-80 was directed against the Mansabdar:
q.x: The 1879-80 Rampa revolt was against Mansabdar Madhava Bhupati and was led by Dwarabandala Chandrayya and Ambul Reddy.

q.s: Which of the following works influenced Gandhi and was written by Leo Tolstoy?
o: The Kingdom of God is Within You
q.x: Tolstoy wrote 'The Kingdom of God is Within You'; 'Unto This Last' is Ruskin's and 'Civil Disobedience' Thoreau's.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT an item of Gandhi's constructive programme?
q.x: The constructive programme covered khadi, prohibition, removal of untouchability, national schools, Hindu-Muslim unity and village panchayats, not heavy industry.

q.s: Ponduru, noted for producing the finest khadi in Andhra Pradesh, is in which district?
q.x: Ponduru in Srikakulam district is famous for its fine khadi.

q.s: Around 1911, roughly what share of the population of the Madras Presidency were Telugus?
q.x: Telugus were about 40% of the Presidency's people but were poorly represented in posts and colleges, which fed the Andhra Movement.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the grievances of the Telugus in the Madras Presidency is correct?
o: Around 1911 no District Judge in the Presidency was a Telugu
In 1915 Andhra had a medical college among its colleges
Around 1911 most District Judges in the Presidency were Telugus
Telugus held more Deputy Collector posts than all others
q.x: No District Judge was a Telugu (0 of 19); Telugus held 21 Deputy Collector posts against 39, and Andhra's 8 colleges had no medical, engineering or law college.

q.s: The Zonal Councils in India were set up under:
q.x: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies created by the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, not by the Constitution.

q.s: How many Zonal Councils were originally created by the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
q.x: The Act created five Zonal Councils; the North Eastern Council came separately in 1971.

q.s: In the first ministry of Andhra Pradesh (1956), the Home portfolio was held by:
q.x: K.V. Ranga Reddy held Home; Bezawada Gopala Reddy held Finance and Kasu Brahmananda Reddy Local Bodies.

q.s: Who among the following was NOT a member of the first ministry of Andhra Pradesh formed in November 1956?
q.x: The first ministry under Neelam Sanjiva Reddy included Gopala Reddy, Ranga Reddy and Sanjivayya; P.V. Narasimha Rao became a minister only in 1962.

q.s: Sikkim became a full-fledged State of the Indian Union through:
q.x: The 36th Amendment (1975) made Sikkim a state; the 35th had made it an associate state.

q.s: The Neolithic site in Kashmir where dogs were buried with their masters is:
q.x: Burzahom is known for pit dwellings and dog burials; Chirand (Bihar) for bone and antler tools.

q.s: Sanganakallu in Ballari district is noted as a Neolithic site with:
q.x: Sanganakallu has ash mounds; the nearby Tekkalakota was excavated by M.S. Nagaraja Rao.

q.s: The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang visited Dhanakataka (Amaravati) in about:
q.x: Hiuen Tsang visited Dhanakataka about 639 CE.

q.s: The place 'Ben Ra' mentioned by Ptolemy has been identified with:
q.x: Ptolemy's Ben Ra is identified with Vengi; the Periplus names the port of Koddura.

q.s: Ushavadatta (Rishabhadatta), known from the Nasik inscriptions, was the son-in-law of the Kshaharata ruler:
q.x: Ushavadatta was Nahapana's son-in-law; Ayama was Nahapana's minister.

q.s: According to the Matsya Purana, the Satavahanas ruled for about:
q.x: The Matsya Purana lists 30 kings ruling 456 years; the Vayu and Vishnu Puranas mention 17 kings and 272 years.

q.s: The ancient port 'Maisolia' mentioned by classical writers is identified with:
q.x: Maisolia is Machilipatnam; Kantakossyla is Ghantasala and Barygaza is Bharuch.

q.s: The ancient port of Kantakossyla on the Andhra coast is identified with:
q.x: Kantakossyla is Ghantasala in Krishna district.

q.s: Which of the following statements about marriage in early Andhra society is correct?
o: Marriage was not regarded as sacred
Marriage was treated as a simple contract
Polygamy existed among the upper classes
q.x: Marriage was a sacred institution, widows observed celibacy and polygamy existed among the upper classes.

q.s: The Ikshvakus of the Krishna valley had their capital at:
q.x: The Ikshvakus ruled from Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda), c. AD 225-300, as successors of the Satavahanas.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri is correct?
o: They were the immediate successors of the Satavahanas in the Krishna valley
They were the immediate predecessors of the Satavahanas
Inscriptions confirm all seven kings named in the Puranas
q.x: The Ikshvakus succeeded the Satavahanas and ruled c. AD 225-300; inscriptions confirm only some Puranic kings.

q.s: Under the Ikshvakus, Brahmadeya grants were exempted from how many taxes?
q.x: Brahmadeya grants were exempt from 18 taxes (ashtadasa parihara).

q.s: Which of the following statements about Ikshvaku society is correct?
o: Ikshvaku records show matronymics and the practice of sati
Brahmins formed the majority of the population
Brahmadeya grants were exempt from 12 taxes
Cross-cousin marriage in Andhra began with the Vishnukundins
q.x: Matronymics and sati appear in Ikshvaku records; Shudras were the majority, brahmadeyas were exempt from 18 taxes, and cross-cousin marriage is linked with the Ikshvakus.

q.s: Lepakshi in Andhra Pradesh is famous for its Veerabhadra temple and:
q.x: Lepakshi has the Veerabhadra temple and a huge monolithic Nandi; it went on UNESCO's tentative list in 2022.

q.s: Which of the following statements about heritage sites in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Lepakshi was placed on the tentative list in 2019
Lepakshi is famous for a Buddhist stupa
Lepakshi is an inscribed UNESCO World Heritage Site
Andhra Pradesh has no inscribed UNESCO World Heritage Site
q.x: AP has no inscribed site; Lepakshi, known for the Veerabhadra temple and monolithic Nandi, went on the tentative list in 2022.

q.s: The Eastern Chalukya ruler associated with the naming of Vijayawada and the building of 108 Shiva temples was:
q.x: Vijayaditya II (Narendra Mriga Raja) is linked with Vijayawada and 108 Shiva temples.

q.s: The Kannada work 'Kavirajamarga' was composed by the Rashtrakuta ruler:
q.x: Kavirajamarga, the earliest Kannada work on poetics, is attributed to Amoghavarsha I.

q.s: The first capital of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi was:
q.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana first ruled from Pishtapura (Pithapuram); Vengi became the later capital.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of old name and present place is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Andhra Nagaram (Dandin) refers to Vengi.

q.s: The first Telugu poetic inscription, composed in the Taruvoja metre, is the:
q.x: The Addanki inscription of Pandaranga is the first Telugu poetic inscription; Kalamalla is the earliest Telugu inscription in prose.

q.s: The title 'Sarvajna Chakravarti' was held by the Reddi ruler:
q.x: Pedakomati Vema, a scholar-king of Kondavidu, was called Sarvajna Chakravarti; Anavota was Dweepa Vijetha.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a capital of the Reddi kingdoms?
q.x: Warangal was the Kakatiya capital.

q.s: Errana (Errapragada), the last of the Kavitrayam, dedicated his Harivamsam to:
q.x: Errana dedicated Harivamsam to Prolaya Vema Reddi, founder of the Reddi kingdom.

q.s: Errana completed the Telugu Mahabharata by writing the remaining part of the:
q.x: Nannaya stopped midway through the Aranya Parva; Tikkana wrote from Virata Parva onwards and Errana completed the Aranya Parva.

q.s: Under the Qutb Shahis, the festival of Muharram came to be popularly celebrated in Andhra as:
q.x: Muharram became Peerla Panduga; Bonalu began at the Mahankali temple in Golconda fort.

q.s: Robert Sewell's 'A Forgotten Empire' (1900) deals with the history of:
q.x: Sewell's work on Vijayanagara carries English translations of Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz.

q.s: Vidyaranya, associated with the founding of Vijayanagara, headed the Shankara Math at:
q.x: Vidyaranya was the head of the Sringeri Math.

q.s: After the Battle of Talikota (1565), the Vijayanagara rulers shifted their capital to:
q.x: Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to Penukonda; Chandragiri and Vellore became capitals later.

q.s: The last ruler of the Tuluva dynasty of Vijayanagara was:
q.x: Sadasiva was the last Tuluva; real power lay with Aliya Rama Raya of the Aravidu family.

q.s: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was built by the Rashtrakuta king:
q.x: The monolithic Kailasa temple was built by Krishna I.

q.s: The Chennakesava temple at Belur was built by the Hoysala king:
q.x: Vishnuvardhana built the Belur temple; the Hoysaleswara temple is at Halebidu.

q.s: Machilipatnam was the principal maritime gateway of which kingdom?
q.x: Machilipatnam was Golconda's main port and passed to the Mughals in 1687.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a port on the Andhra coast?
q.x: Surat was the Mughal port on the west coast in Gujarat.

q.s: The attack on the British Residency at Hyderabad on 17 July 1857 was led by Maulvi Allauddin and:
q.x: Turrebaz Khan and Maulvi Allauddin attacked to free Jamedar Chida Khan; they were repulsed by Resident Col. Davidson.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the attack on the Hyderabad Residency (1857) is correct?
o: Turrebaz Khan was shot near Aurangabad
For its loyalty Hyderabad got back Berar
Maulvi Allauddin was transported to the Andamans
It was repulsed by Resident James Kirkpatrick
q.x: Allauddin was transported and died in the Andamans (1884); the Resident was Col. Davidson, Turrebaz Khan was shot near Toopran, and Hyderabad got back the Raichur Doab and Dharashiv.

q.s: The Kotappakonda riots of February 1909, during the Vandemataram movement, took place near:
q.x: Kotappakonda is near Narasaraopet; Chinnapa Reddy got the only death sentence of the movement.

q.s: The Andhra Rashtra Kisan Congress was formed in 1943 by:
q.x: N.G. Ranga formed it after leaving the communist-led AIKS over its pro-war line.

q.s: The 1935 Guntur anti-resettlement movement (Peasant Protection Rally) was led by:
q.x: Ranga led it; M.N. Roy addressed the 1937 Nellore labourers' meeting.

q.s: The first Mahasabha of the Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad was held in 1929 at:
q.x: It was held at Tenali; the Parishad also brought out the magazine Natya Kala.

q.s: Which of the following statements about theatre bodies in Andhra is correct?
o: Land for the Lalita Kala Parishad, Anantapur was given by Kalluru Subbarao
The first Mahasabha of the Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad was held at Rajahmundry
The Lalita Kala Parishad, Anantapur brought out the magazine Natya Kala
The Nataka Vidyalayam at Vijayawada was set up in 1956
q.x: Kalluru Subbarao gave the land; the first Mahasabha was at Tenali, the Nataka Vidyalayam came in 1964 and Natya Kala was the Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad's magazine.

q.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was convicted for sedition in 1908 for his writings in the paper:
q.x: His Swarajya writings brought a three-year sentence under Section 124A, making him the first Telugu journalist jailed for sedition in South India.

q.s: The Greyhounds, Andhra Pradesh's elite anti-Naxal force, was raised in:
q.x: The Greyhounds were raised in 1989; the People's War Group was banned in 1992.

q.s: The First Battle of Tarain (1191) arose over Muhammad Ghori's attack on:
q.x: Ghori had taken Tabarhinda, which Prithviraj sought to recover; Prithviraj won in 1191 but lost in 1192.

q.s: In Javed v. State of Haryana (2003), the Supreme Court:
o: Referred the two-child norm to a larger bench
Struck down the two-child norm for local body polls
Extended the two-child norm to Assembly elections
Upheld the two-child norm for local body polls
q.x: The Court upheld the two-child norm; Andhra Pradesh later removed its norm (dating from 1994) through Bills in 2024.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the two-child norm is correct?
o: The Supreme Court struck it down in Javed v. State of Haryana (2003)
Andhra Pradesh's norm for local body polls dated from 1994 and was removed by Bills in 2024
Andhra Pradesh introduced the norm for local bodies in 2014
Andhra Pradesh's 2026 draft population policy penalises a third child
q.x: AP's 1994 norm was removed in 2024 and its 2026 draft policy offers incentives for more children; the Supreme Court had upheld the norm in Javed.

q.s: The rule of marrying outside one's own gotra or clan is known as:
q.x: Exogamy is marriage outside the group; endogamy is marriage within it. The incest taboo underlies exogamy.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a rule of choosing a marriage partner?
q.x: Polyandry is a form of marriage (one wife, several husbands); endogamy, exogamy and hypergamy are rules of mate selection.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT among the four approved forms of marriage in the Manu Smriti?
q.x: Gandharva marriage (mutual consent, as of Shakuntala and Dushyanta) is a disapproved form; Brahma, Daiva, Arsha and Prajapatya are the approved forms.

q.s: Herbert Risley ranked castes according to social precedence in the Census of:
q.x: Risley, Census Commissioner, ranked castes in 1901 and gave the racial theory of caste.

q.s: Which of the following statements about theories of caste is correct?
o: Herbert Risley ranked castes by social precedence in the 1931 Census
Abbe Dubois explained caste as a product of race
The racial theory of caste was given by S.V. Ketkar
S.V. Ketkar held that caste membership is by birth, with a bar on marrying outside the group
q.x: Ketkar's 'History of Caste in India' (1909) stressed birth and endogamy; Risley ranked castes in 1901 and gave the racial theory, while Dubois saw caste as a Brahmin device.

q.s: The book 'India's Silent Revolution', on the rise of lower castes through politics, was written by:
q.x: Jaffrelot argued that lower castes are rising through politics; M.N. Srinivas gave the idea of Sanskritisation.

q.s: According to the 2011 Census, the urban share of Andhra Pradesh's population (13 districts) was about:
q.x: Urban share rose from 24.13% in 2001 to 29.47% in 2011.

q.s: According to the 2011 Census, the most urbanised of Andhra Pradesh's old 13 districts was:
q.x: Visakhapatnam (47.45%) was the most urbanised and Srikakulam (16.16%) the least.

q.s: The State with the highest number of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) in India is:
q.x: Odisha has 13 PVTGs, the highest; undivided Andhra Pradesh comes next.

q.s: The category 'Primitive Tribal Groups' was renamed 'Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups' in:
q.x: The PTG category was created in 1973 and renamed PVTG in 2006.

q.s: The Oraon (Kurukh) tribe belongs to which language family?
q.x: Oraons speak Kurukh, a Dravidian language; the Khasi are Austro-Asiatic and the Nyishi Tibeto-Burman.

q.s: Which of the following tribes does NOT belong to the Austro-Asiatic (Munda) language group?
q.x: Oraons speak Kurukh, a Dravidian language.

q.s: The Renke Commission (2008) dealt with:
q.x: The Renke Commission dealt with denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic tribes; the Idate Commission followed in 2017.

q.s: Which of the following statements about denotified tribes is correct?
o: The Idate Commission on denotified tribes was set up in 2017
The Renke Commission dealt with PVTGs
The Criminal Tribes Act was replaced by the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
Denotified tribes have been counted separately in every Census since Independence
q.x: The Idate Commission came in 2017; Renke dealt with DNTs, they were last counted in 1931, and the CTA was replaced by Habitual Offenders Acts.

q.s: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, which replaced the Sarda Act of 1929, was enacted in:
q.x: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act is of 2006; the PCPNDT Act is of 1994.

q.s: The Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act was passed in:
q.x: The Sati (Prevention) Act came in 1987 after the Roop Kanwar case; the Indecent Representation of Women Act is of 1986.

q.s: The Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW) was adopted by the UN in:
q.x: CEDAW was adopted in 1979; India signed in 1980 and ratified in 1993.

q.s: Which of the following cities did NOT host a UN World Conference on Women?
q.x: The conferences were held at Mexico City (1975), Copenhagen (1980), Nairobi (1985) and Beijing (1995).

q.s: Which Five-Year Plan shifted the approach to women from 'development' to 'empowerment'?
q.x: The Eighth Plan made the shift to empowerment; the Sixth had moved from welfare to development.

q.s: The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme was launched in:
q.x: BBBP was launched in 2015; the Mission for Empowerment of Women dates from 2010.

q.s: The Safai Karmachari Andolan, a movement against manual scavenging, was co-founded by:
q.x: Bezwada Wilson co-founded it and won the Magsaysay Award in 2016; Bindeshwar Pathak founded Sulabh International.

q.s: Which of the following bodies is NOT meant for the welfare of Scheduled Castes or sanitation workers?
q.x: NSTFDC is the National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation.

q.s: The 'Mulki rules' were related to:
o: Job preference for local residents in Hyderabad/Telangana
q.x: Mulki rules gave job preference to local residents of Hyderabad State/Telangana.

q.s: Under the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, the minimum punishment for rape was raised from 7 years to:
q.x: The 2018 Act raised the minimum to 10 years and barred anticipatory bail for rape of a girl below 16.

q.s: The 'NATO' classification of the tools of government (Nodality, Authority, Treasure, Organisation) was given by:
q.x: Christopher Hood gave the NATO scheme; nudges come from Thaler and Sunstein's behavioural design.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of Christopher Hood's 'NATO' tools of government?
q.x: NATO stands for Nodality, Authority, Treasure and Organisation.

q.s: The Central Social Welfare Board was set up in:
q.x: The CSWB was set up in 1953.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 is correct?
o: It requires one old age home in each State only
Only biological children are liable to maintain parents
It came into force on the same date in all States
Adopted and step-children are also liable to maintain parents
q.x: 'Children' include adopted and step-children; the Act came into force State by State and requires at least one old age home per district.

q.s: Which of the following is an accessible-elections measure for persons with disabilities?
q.x: Braille signage on EVMs helps visually impaired voters; the other options are general electoral features.

q.s: The 'India Out' campaign is associated with the domestic politics of:
q.x: 'India Out' was a Maldivian campaign; India also funds the Greater Male Connectivity bridge-causeway there.

q.s: The exercise 'Indra' is a tri-service military exercise between India and:
q.x: Indra is with Russia; JIMEX is with Japan (Navy) and Garuda with France (Air Force).

q.s: 'Desert Knight' is an air exercise of India with:
q.x: Desert Knight involves the Air Forces of India, France and the UAE.

q.s: The Bretton Woods Conference of July 1944, which created the IMF and the World Bank, was held in:
q.x: It met at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, with 44 allied nations; Harry Dexter White's plan was preferred to Keynes's.

q.s: Which institution planned at Bretton Woods was never created, its gap being filled by GATT (1947)?
o: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
q.x: The ITO never came into being; GATT served until the WTO was set up in 1995.

q.s: The COVID-19 TRIPS waiver proposal at the WTO in 2020 was moved by India and:
q.x: India and South Africa proposed the waiver; MC12 (2022) agreed a limited waiver for vaccine patents.

q.s: Under UNCLOS, the contiguous zone of a coastal State extends up to:
q.x: The territorial sea is 12 nm, the contiguous zone 24 nm and the EEZ 200 nm.

q.s: India's 'Samudrayaan' mission with the submersible Matsya-6000 is part of:
q.x: Samudrayaan belongs to the Ministry of Earth Sciences' Deep Ocean Mission.

q.s: The Right to Property under Article 300A of the Constitution is at present a:
q.x: The 44th Amendment removed property from Fundamental Rights and placed it in Article 300A as a constitutional right.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
q.x: NITI Aayog was set up by a Cabinet resolution; the other three are created by the Constitution.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Financial Emergency under Article 360 is correct?
o: It applies only to a threat to the whole of India
It has been proclaimed once, in 1991
It cannot cover salaries of Supreme Court judges
State Money Bills may be reserved for the President's consideration
q.x: During a Financial Emergency State Money and Financial Bills may be reserved for the President; it has never been declared, and salaries of all Union servants, including judges, can be cut.

q.s: The 97th Constitutional Amendment (2011) added the right to form co-operative societies to:
q.x: It added co-operatives to Article 19(1)(c), inserted Article 43B and Part IXB.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the 97th Constitutional Amendment is correct?
o: It placed co-operatives in the Concurrent List
It inserted Article 43B and Part IXB
It added co-operative societies to Article 19(1)(g)
q.x: The 97th Amendment (2011) added co-operatives to Article 19(1)(c), inserted Article 43B (DPSP) and Part IXB.

q.s: Article 15(4) was inserted by the First Amendment (1951) to nullify the judgment in:
o: State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan
q.x: The Champakam Dorairajan case struck down communal reservation in Madras; the 1st Amendment added Article 15(4).

q.s: Consequential seniority for SCs/STs promoted through reservation was provided by the:
q.x: The 85th Amendment gave consequential seniority; the 82nd allowed relaxation of qualifying marks and the 89th created the NCST.

q.s: Under the Supreme Court's 'triple test' for OBC reservation in local bodies, total reservation must not exceed:
q.x: The triple test needs a dedicated commission, a local-body-wise proportion and total reservation within 50 per cent.

q.s: The eleventh Fundamental Duty (education of children aged 6-14) was added by the:
q.x: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added Article 51A(k); the original ten duties came from the 42nd Amendment.

q.s: The Fundamental Duties were included in the Constitution on the recommendation of the:
q.x: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended them; the 42nd Amendment inserted them.

q.s: Disputes relating to the election of the Vice-President are decided by:
q.x: Under Article 71, such disputes are decided by the Supreme Court.

q.s: Within how many days must the Rajya Sabha return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha?
q.x: The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill within 14 days, with or without recommendations.

q.s: A no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers can be moved in:
q.x: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, so the motion lies only there.

q.s: Since 2014, the day's sitting in the Rajya Sabha begins with:
q.x: In the Rajya Sabha Zero Hour is at 11 AM and Question Hour 12 Noon-1 PM; in the Lok Sabha Question Hour comes first.

q.s: Which of the following motions can be moved only in the Lok Sabha?
q.x: The adjournment motion, which involves censure, is confined to the Lok Sabha; calling attention can be moved in either House.

q.s: The All India Presiding Officers' Conference (AIPOC) has been held since:
q.x: The AIPOC dates from 1921; its 86th session was at Lucknow.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about a State Legislative Council?
o: Its members have a six-year term
One-third of its members retire every second year
The Governor can dissolve it on the CM's advice
q.x: The Council cannot be dissolved; Parliament may abolish it under Article 169 on the Assembly's resolution.

q.s: The oath of office of the President of India is administered by:
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
q.x: The CJI (or in his absence the senior-most Supreme Court judge) administers the President's oath.

q.s: The executive power of the State is vested in the Governor under:
q.x: Article 154 vests the State's executive power in the Governor; Article 168 makes the Governor part of the State Legislature.

q.s: The Governor of a State takes the oath of office before:
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
q.x: Under Article 159 the oath is taken before the Chief Justice of the High Court or the senior-most judge.

q.s: The Committee of Privileges of the Rajya Sabha is chaired by:
q.x: The Deputy Chairman heads the 10-member Rajya Sabha committee; the Lok Sabha committee has 15 members nominated by the Speaker.

q.s: Which of the following statements about parliamentary privileges is correct?
o: The Lok Sabha Committee of Privileges has 10 members
They are codified in a single statute of Parliament
The Rajya Sabha Committee of Privileges is chaired by the Chairman
In a breach of privilege case, the final decision is taken by the House
q.x: The House decides; privileges are uncodified, the RS committee is chaired by the Deputy Chairman and the LS committee has 15 members.

q.s: A judge of a High Court addresses his resignation in writing to:
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
q.x: Under Article 217(1)(a) a High Court judge resigns by writing to the President.

q.s: The retirement age of High Court judges was raised from 60 to 62 by the:
q.x: The 15th Amendment (1963) raised it to 62; the 114th Amendment Bill (2010) sought 65.

q.s: The allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to the States and Union Territories is laid down in the:
q.x: The Fourth Schedule allots seats; Uttar Pradesh has the most, 31.

q.s: Which of the following features of the US federation is NOT found in the Indian federation?
o: Equal representation of States in the Upper House
q.x: Rajya Sabha seats vary with population (UP has 31); equal representation is a US Senate feature.

q.s: The residuary powers of legislation are vested in Parliament under:
q.x: Article 248 (Part XI) vests residuary powers, including residuary taxation, in Parliament.

q.s: Which committee recommended that residuary powers be transferred to the States?
q.x: The Tamil Nadu-appointed Rajamannar Committee (1969) wanted residuary powers given to the States.

q.s: The qualifications of the members of the Finance Commission are laid down in:
q.x: Article 280 lets Parliament fix qualifications, which it did by the 1951 Act; the Chairman must have experience in public affairs.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the members of the Finance Commission is correct?
o: Their qualifications are laid down in Article 280 itself
Ten years as an MP is a qualification for a member
The Chairman must be a judge of a High Court
Members hold office as the President specifies and are eligible for reappointment
q.x: Members serve as the President specifies and can be reappointed; qualifications are in the 1951 Act and the Chairman needs experience in public affairs.

q.s: The delimitation of Jammu and Kashmir completed in 2022 was done by a Commission headed by:
q.x: The Justice Ranjana Desai Commission delimited J&K; Assam was delimited by the Election Commission itself in 2023.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Election Commission is correct?
o: Officers on election duty work under the control of the Election Commission
The J&K delimitation of 2022 was done by the Kuldip Singh Commission
Assam's 2023 delimitation was done by the Ranjana Desai Commission
Officers on election duty remain under the sole control of State governments
q.x: The EC controls officers on election duty and can transfer or suspend them; it delimited Assam itself, and J&K was done by the Ranjana Desai Commission.

q.s: The National Human Rights Commission of India is a:
o: Statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
Executive body under a Cabinet resolution
q.x: The NHRC was set up under the PHRA, 1993, in line with the Paris Principles.

q.s: The Paris Principles relating to national human rights institutions were adopted by the UN General Assembly in:
q.x: They were drafted in Paris in 1991 and adopted by the UNGA in 1993.

q.s: The Central Information Commission was constituted in 2005 under which section of the RTI Act?
q.x: Section 12 constitutes the CIC; Section 15 deals with State Information Commissions.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Information Commissions is correct?
o: A State Information Commissioner is removed after an inquiry by the Supreme Court
A State Information Commissioner is removed after an inquiry by the High Court
The CIC can have up to fifteen Information Commissioners
The 2019 Rules set the term at five years
q.x: Removal needs a Supreme Court inquiry; the CIC has up to ten commissioners and the 2019 Rules set a three-year term.

q.s: Under the RTI Act, 2005, penalties on Public Information Officers are provided in:
q.x: Section 20 deals with penalties; Section 6(2) says no reason need be given for seeking information.

q.s: Section 17A, which requires prior approval before investigating certain decisions of public servants, is a provision of the:
q.x: Section 17A was added to the Prevention of Corruption Act in 2018.

q.s: A key weakness of many State Lokayuktas is that they:
o: Have no power to receive complaints
Are appointed by the Prime Minister
q.x: Many depend on the State police or Anti-Corruption Bureau for investigation, which limits their independence.

q.s: Under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014, the competent authority for disclosures about central government employees is the:
q.x: The CVC is the competent authority; anonymous complaints are not entertained.

q.s: Which of the following statements on Governor-State conflicts is correct?
o: The Kurian Joseph Committee was set up by the Union Government
The 20 November 2025 Presidential Reference opinion upheld 'deemed assent'
The Supreme Court has never ruled on Governor's assent to Bills
In State of Tamil Nadu v Governor (April 2025), the Supreme Court laid down timelines and 'deemed assent'
q.x: The April 2025 judgment set timelines and deemed assent; the November 2025 opinion rejected court-imposed timelines and deemed assent. The Kurian Joseph Committee was set up by Tamil Nadu.

q.s: Political parties in India are recognised as national or State parties by the Election Commission under:
o: The Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968
q.x: Recognition is under the Symbols Order, 1968; Section 29A deals with registration.

q.s: Which of the following parties lost national party status in 2023?
q.x: The AITC, NCP and CPI lost national status in 2023; AAP gained it.

q.s: Which committee suggested a list of subjects for Panchayati Raj institutions that became the basis of the Eleventh Schedule?
q.x: The Thungon Committee (1988) suggested the subject list; Dantwala (1978) stressed block-level planning.

q.s: Which of the following committees is NOT related to Panchayati Raj?
q.x: The Kothari Commission (1964-66) dealt with education.

q.s: Which new criterion, carrying 10% weight, was introduced by the Sixteenth Finance Commission in place of tax effort?
q.x: Contribution to GDP replaced tax effort; income distance still carries the highest weight.

q.s: NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index uses how many indicators?
q.x: The National MPI uses 12 indicators, adding maternal health and bank account to the Global MPI's 10.

q.s: Which of the following indices is NOT brought out by NITI Aayog?
q.x: The HDI is published by UNDP.

q.s: The National Development Council (NDC) was set up on 6 August 1952 by:
o: An executive order of the Government
q.x: The NDC was a non-statutory body created by executive order; the Planning Commission's Secretary was its Secretary.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the National Development Council?
q.x: The CJI was never a member of the NDC.

q.s: Applying for an income certificate through MeeSeva or UMANG is an example of which type of e-governance interaction?
q.x: It is Government-to-Citizen; GSTN and e-Procurement are G2B, while SWAN and e-Office are G2G.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of Government-to-Government (G2G) interaction?
q.x: GSTN serves businesses, a G2B interaction.

q.s: The Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) in India works on the single emergency number:
q.x: ERSS integrates police, fire and ambulance services under 112.

q.s: The Digital India programme, launched on 1 July 2015, is implemented by the:
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
q.x: MeitY implements Digital India; its nine pillars include e-Kranti and Early Harvest Programmes.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the nine pillars of the Digital India programme?
q.x: There is no satellite launch pillar; the pillars include Broadband Highways, e-Kranti and Early Harvest Programmes.

q.s: The Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (MKSS), whose campaign paved the way for the RTI Act, 2005, was led by:
q.x: Aruna Roy and Nikhil Dey led MKSS; Medha Patkar led the Narmada Bachao Andolan.

q.s: The India Against Corruption movement of 2011 was led by:
q.x: Anna Hazare led the movement that resulted in the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, sanction of new projects on the Krishna and Godavari rests with the:
q.x: The Apex Council clears new projects; water shares are allocated by tribunals, and the Boards regulate supply from notified projects.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Allocating the States' shares of river water
Regulating water and power supply from notified projects
Implementing tribunal awards for notified projects
Advising the States on flood and drought management
q.x: Water shares are allocated by tribunals; new projects are cleared by the Apex Council.

q.s: The India State of Forest Report (ISFR) is published by the Forest Survey of India:
q.x: The ISFR is biennial; forest cover means land with canopy density of 10% or more.

q.s: Which State ranks first in Recorded Forest Area in India?
q.x: Madhya Pradesh is first; Andhra Pradesh ranks 8th.

q.s: Which Census year is known as the 'Year of the Great Divide' in India's population history?
q.x: 1921 recorded the only negative decadal growth (-0.31%); population grew steadily after it.

q.s: In the RBI's typology of States by demographic phase, which of the following are in the 'ageing' phase?
q.x: Kerala and Tamil Nadu are ageing; Telangana and Uttarakhand are in the narrowing-window phase.

q.s: The urban heat island effect is most pronounced:
q.x: Cities release stored heat at night, so the temperature gap with the countryside is largest then.

q.s: Among India's million-plus cities, the highest share of slum population (about 44%) was found in:
q.x: Greater Visakhapatnam had about 44% of its people in slums, the highest among million-plus cities.

q.s: In Swachh Survekshan 2023, the cleanest city in Andhra Pradesh, ranked 4th in India, was:
q.x: Visakhapatnam was 4th nationally and AP's cleanest in 2023; Vijayawada later entered the Super Swachh League.

q.s: The Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (1999) replaced the individual-family approach of IRDP with:
q.x: SGSY organised the rural poor into SHGs with group financing; IRDP had targeted individual families.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a self-employment programme for the rural poor?
q.x: MGNREGA is a wage employment guarantee programme.

q.s: The Atal Pension Yojana guarantees a monthly pension at the age of 60 in the range of:
q.x: APY is a defined-benefit scheme guaranteeing Rs 1,000-5,000 a month; the Government co-contributed 50% (up to Rs 1,000) for early joiners.

q.s: Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas (DWCRA), started in 1982-83, was a sub-scheme of:
q.x: DWCRA was a sub-scheme of IRDP; in AP it was later merged with Velugu as Indira Kranthi Patham under SERP.

q.s: In 1950-51, the share of the services sector in India's GDP was about:
q.x: Services were about 30.3% of GDP in 1950-51, rising to over 50% by 2000-01 and about 54% now.

q.s: The theme of UNDP's Human Development Report 2025 is:
o: A Matter of Choice: People and Possibilities in the Age of AI
q.x: HDR 2025 deals with AI; HDR 2023-24 was 'Breaking the Gridlock' and 2021/22 'Uncertain Times, Unsettled Lives'.

q.s: According to ISRO's Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas (2021), the leading process of land degradation in India is:
q.x: Water erosion leads (about 11% of area), followed by vegetation degradation.

q.s: Which of the following statements about land degradation in India (ISRO Atlas, 2021) is correct?
o: India restored about 21.76 Mha of land during 2011-2020
Vegetation degradation is the leading process
About half of India's area is degraded
q.x: India restored 21.76 Mha in 2011-20; desertification rose in 28 States/UTs, water erosion leads, and about 29.77% (97.85 Mha) is degraded.

q.s: The National Planning Committee of 1938 was chaired by:
q.x: It was set up under Congress President Subhas Bose and chaired by Nehru.

q.s: The 'People's Plan' of 1945 was prepared by:
q.x: M.N. Roy prepared the People's Plan; the Gandhian Plan was by Shriman Narayan and the Bombay Plan by industrialists.

q.s: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015 through:
q.x: NITI Aayog was set up by a Cabinet resolution, like the Planning Commission before it.

q.s: The Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) was replaced by the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) in:
q.x: FEMA was enacted in 1999 (in force 2000); LERMS came in 1992 and current account convertibility in 1994.

q.s: The Liberalised Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS) was introduced in:
q.x: LERMS (1992) gave a dual rate; a unified market-determined rate followed in 1993.

q.s: In the Sustainable Development Report 2025 of SDSN, India's rank was:
q.x: India was 99th of 167 in SDR 2025, its first entry into the top 100; it was 112th in 2023.

q.s: In NITI Aayog's SDG India Index, a State is classed as an 'Achiever' when its score is:
q.x: Only a score of 100 earns 'Achiever'; 65-99 is Front Runner and 50-64 Performer.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the SDG India Index 2023-24 is correct?
o: The raw data are normalised to a 0-100 scale
A composite score of 60 makes a State a Front Runner
A score of 90 makes a State an Achiever
q.x: Data are normalised to 0-100; only 16 goals were scored, 60 is a Performer score and only 100 makes an Achiever.

q.s: The number of times a unit of money changes hands in a given period is called:
q.x: This is the velocity of money; the money multiplier relates money supply to reserve money.

q.s: The Digital Rupee (e-Rupee) was given legal tender status by amending the:
q.x: The Finance Act, 2022 amended the RBI Act to include digital currency.

q.s: The Economic Capital Framework of the RBI was recommended by the committee headed by:
q.x: The Bimal Jalan Committee (2019) set the framework that decides the RBI's surplus transfer.

q.s: The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India is appointed by the Central Government for a term of up to:
q.x: The Governor's term is up to 5 years; directors of the 21-member Central Board serve 4 years.

q.s: Which of the following activities can a payments bank in India NOT undertake?
q.x: Payments banks cannot lend or issue credit cards; they can take deposits, issue debit cards and handle remittances.

q.s: Under the RBI's 2014 guidelines, the minimum paid-up capital of a small finance bank was:
q.x: It was Rs 100 crore in 2014, later raised to Rs 200 crore; SFBs must lend 75% of ANBC to the priority sector.

q.s: Andhra Bank, founded in 1923 by Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya, had its origin at:
q.x: Andhra Bank was founded at Machilipatnam; it merged with Union Bank of India in 2020.

q.s: Canara Bank was founded in 1906 at:
q.x: Canara Bank was founded at Mangaluru; Punjab National Bank was founded at Lahore in 1894.

q.s: Since 1 April 2012, a cheque in India is valid for a period of:
q.x: The RBI cut cheque validity from six to three months from 1 April 2012.

q.s: Which of the following statements about commercial banking is correct?
o: Deposits accepted from customers are a liability of a commercial bank
Factoring is a core banking activity, not para-banking
Deposits are an asset of a commercial bank
Since 2012 a cheque is valid for six months
q.x: Deposits are liabilities; cheques are valid for three months since 2012 and factoring, insurance and credit cards are para-banking.

q.s: The East Asian financial crisis of 1997 began with the collapse of the:
q.x: It began in Thailand when the baht was floated in July 1997.

q.s: The 'taper tantrum' of 2013 was triggered by signals from:
q.x: The US Fed's hint at tapering asset purchases caused capital outflows; the rupee fell about 17%.

q.s: Off-budget borrowings of the Government are criticised mainly because they:
o: Cannot be used for capital spending
Are borrowed only from the RBI
Are serviced only by foreign lenders
Hide the true level of public debt and deficit
q.x: Loans raised through PSUs or SPVs are serviced from the budget but kept outside the deficit, understating debt.

q.s: The Net Barter Terms of Trade of a country is the ratio of:
o: Import price index to export price index
Export quantity index to import quantity index
Export price index to import price index
q.x: NTT = (export price index / import price index) x 100; gross terms relate import and export quantities.

q.s: The FDI limit in public sector banks in India is:
q.x: FDI in PSBs is capped at 20% through the Government route; telecom allows 100% automatic.

q.s: FDI in the defence sector through the automatic route is permitted up to:
q.x: Defence allows 74% automatic and up to 100% through the Government route.

q.s: The PM POSHAN (Mid-Day Meal) scheme is implemented by the:
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
q.x: PM POSHAN is under the Ministry of Education; ICDS is under the Ministry of WCD.

q.s: The Minimum Support Price for crops is recommended by the:
o: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices
q.x: The CACP recommends MSP; the FCI procures and sells under OMSS.

q.s: Minimum buffer stock norms for the central pool are fixed for each quarter by the:
q.x: The CCEA fixes the norms; the strategic reserve is held over and above operational stocks.

q.s: Which State is called the 'Rice Bowl of central India'?
q.x: Chhattisgarh is known as the Rice Bowl of central India.

q.s: Which State is the largest producer of milk in India?
q.x: Uttar Pradesh leads, followed by Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat.

q.s: The Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses promises 100% MSP procurement of:
q.x: The mission (2025-26 to 2030-31, Rs 11,440 crore) assures procurement of tur, urad and masoor.

q.s: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana focuses on:
o: Only rainfed districts of central India
q.x: PMDDKY covers 100 districts with low productivity, low cropping intensity and low credit.

q.s: The Ninth Schedule, to protect land reform laws from judicial review, was added to the Constitution by the:
q.x: The First Amendment added Articles 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule; the 25th added Article 31C.

q.s: The main cause of the 'feminisation of agriculture' in rural India is:
o: Male out-migration to non-farm and urban work
q.x: As men move to non-farm and urban jobs, women's share among cultivators and labourers rises; ownership remains largely with men.

q.s: The ideal N:P:K ratio recommended for balanced fertiliser use in India is:
q.x: The ideal is 4:2:1; the actual skewed ratio has been about 10.9:4.1:1.

q.s: Small and marginal holdings account for about what share of operational holdings in India?
q.x: About 86% of holdings are small and marginal.

q.s: Under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme, the effective interest rate on short-term crop loans for prompt repayers is:
q.x: The base rate is 7%; 1.5% subvention to lenders and 3% prompt repayment incentive bring it to 4%.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme is correct?
o: The effective rate for prompt repayers is 7%
Its loan limit was raised to Rs 3 lakh in August 2026
Lending institutions get 1.5% interest subvention on short-term crop loans
It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme run by State cooperative departments
q.x: Lenders get 1.5%; prompt repayers pay 4%, MISS is a Central Sector scheme through RBI and NABARD, and the limit went from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 5 lakh.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, urban Self Help Groups are handled by:
q.x: MEPMA handles urban SHGs and SERP rural SHGs; AP has about 36% of India's SHG-bank linkage.

q.s: Which of the following statements about SHG credit in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: SHGs must be registered before bank linkage
Andhra Pradesh has about 36% of India's SHG-bank linkage
SERP handles urban SHGs in the State
Each SHG member needs a CIBIL credit history for bank linkage
q.x: AP has about a 36% share; SERP is rural, MEPMA urban, and neither registration nor individual CIBIL history is needed.

q.s: Under the RBI's revised Kisan Credit Card Directions of June 2026, the maximum KCC tenure is raised to:
q.x: The Directions raise the tenure to six years and apply to loans from 1 January 2027.

q.s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, Schedule A listed industries that were:
o: Jointly run by Centre and States
The exclusive responsibility of the State
Left entirely to the private sector
q.x: Schedule A had 17 industries exclusively for the State; Schedule B had 12 to be progressively State-owned.

q.s: Under the 1956 Resolution, how many industries were placed in Schedule A?
q.x: Schedule A had 17 industries and Schedule B 12.

q.s: Which of the following statements about electronics manufacturing schemes is correct?
o: The ECMS outlay was raised to Rs 40,000 crore in Budget 2026-27
The Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme replaces the ECMS
The ECMS was discontinued in Budget 2026-27
The Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme gives no incentive for domestic sourcing
q.x: The ECMS continues with Rs 40,000 crore; the new mobile scheme replaces the PLI for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing and offers up to 1.5% extra for domestic sourcing.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a category of loans under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana?
q.x: PMMY has Shishu, Kishor, Tarun and Tarun Plus; loans are collateral-free up to Rs 20 lakh.

q.s: A deep-tech startup in India can be recognised for up to how many years from incorporation?
q.x: Deep-tech entities get up to 20 years; ordinary startups up to 10 years with a Rs 200 crore turnover limit.

q.s: Under PM Vishwakarma, collateral-free credit is provided at a concessional interest rate of:
q.x: PM Vishwakarma gives credit up to Rs 3 lakh at 5% and a training stipend of Rs 500 a day.

q.s: The Sick Industrial Companies Act (SICA), 1985 and the BIFR were based on the recommendations of the:
q.x: The Tiwari Committee (1984-85) led to SICA and the BIFR; the Eradi Committee proposed the NCLT.

q.s: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 was based on the report of the Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee headed by:
q.x: T.K. Viswanathan headed the BLRC (2015), whose draft became the IBC, 2016.

q.s: In 2024-25, the largest sub-sector of Andhra Pradesh's agriculture and allied GVA among the following was:
q.x: Livestock had about 12% share of GVA, horticulture 10%, crops 4% and forestry 1%.

q.s: The fiscal deficit of a government is equal to:
o: Revenue deficit plus net capital spending
Total expenditure minus revenue receipts including borrowings
q.x: Fiscal deficit = revenue deficit + capital outlay and net lending - non-debt capital receipts; so it exceeds the revenue deficit when the State invests.

q.s: ICAR's Central Tobacco Research Institute (CTRI) is located at:
q.x: ICAR-CTRI is at Rajahmundry; the oil palm institute (IIOPR) is at Pedavegi.

q.s: Dr YSR Horticultural University of Andhra Pradesh is located at:
q.x: It is at Venkataramannagudem in West Godavari; the Indo-Israel CoE for vegetables is at Kuppam.

q.s: The Murrah breed, used for grading up buffaloes in Andhra Pradesh, originated in:
q.x: Murrah is a Haryana buffalo breed; graded Murrah buffaloes and crossbred cattle support AP's milk output.

q.s: The headquarters of the Godavari agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh is at:
q.x: The Godavari Zone is based at Maruteru; Anakapalle is the North Coastal Zone HQ and Lam the Krishna Zone HQ.

q.s: The Rythu Bazars of Andhra Pradesh, started in 1999, allow:
o: Direct sale by farmers to consumers
q.x: Rythu Bazars let farmers sell directly to consumers; they are outside the Agricultural Market Committees.

q.s: The Pattiseema scheme in Andhra Pradesh is a lift irrigation scheme that links the Godavari with the:
q.x: Pattiseema lifts Godavari water into the Polavaram right canal to reach the Krishna, as a stop-gap till Polavaram's gravity flow starts.

q.s: The National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB) is headquartered at:
q.x: NFDB is at Hyderabad; MPEDA is at Kochi.

q.s: Which country is the second largest fish producer in the world?
q.x: India is second after China, which produces about 36% of world fish.

q.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's industrial policy, Mega projects may receive investment subsidy of up to:
q.x: Mega projects get up to 15% and Large projects up to 12%.

q.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's MSME & Entrepreneur Development Policy (4.0) 2024-29, MSME parks are planned:
q.x: The policy plans 175+ MSME parks, one in each Assembly constituency, and targets Rs 50,000 crore investment.

q.s: Multimodal logistics parks at Visakhapatnam and Ananthapur are being developed under:
q.x: Multimodal logistics parks come under Bharatmala Pariyojana.

q.s: The Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP) has been a Central Sector scheme with 100% central funding since:
q.x: DILRMP became a Central Sector scheme from 1 April 2016; it began as NLRMP merging CLR and SRA&ULR.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme is correct?
o: It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with 60:40 funding
A gender column in the Record of Rights has been made optional
It began by merging MGNREGA and PMAY-G
A gender column in the Record of Rights has been made mandatory
q.x: The gender column is mandatory; DILRMP is a 100% centrally funded Central Sector scheme that began as NLRMP by merging CLR and SRA&ULR.

q.s: India imports coking coal mainly because:
o: Coal imports are banned except for coking coal
Domestic high-quality, low-ash coking coal is limited
q.x: Indian coal is high in ash; steel needs low-ash coking coal, so it is imported.

q.s: Marble is a metamorphic rock formed from:
q.x: Limestone becomes marble; shale becomes slate and granite becomes gneiss.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of parent rock and metamorphic rock is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Limestone becomes marble; amphibolite forms from basalt.

q.s: A rift valley is formed by:
q.x: Tension creates down-faulted grabens or rift valleys; uplifted blocks (horsts) form block mountains.

q.s: Which of the following is an example of a block mountain?
q.x: The Sierra Nevada is an uplifted fault block; the Himalayas and Andes are fold mountains and Fuji is volcanic.

q.s: The concept that mountains have deep 'roots' to maintain isostatic balance was put forward by:
q.x: Airy assumed uniform density, so higher mountains must have deeper roots; Pratt assumed varying density.

q.s: Which is the smallest ocean in the world?
q.x: The Arctic is the smallest; the Pacific is the largest and the Atlantic second.

q.s: Oceans cover about what percentage of the Earth's surface?
q.x: Oceans cover about 70-71% of the Earth's surface.

q.s: The Tibetan plateau is an example of which type of plateau?
q.x: It is enclosed by mountains, hence intermontane; Patagonia is piedmont and the Columbia plateau volcanic.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an intermontane plateau?
q.x: Patagonia is a piedmont plateau.

q.s: Lines on a map joining places having equal atmospheric pressure are called:
q.x: Isobars join points of equal pressure; closely spaced isobars mean a steep gradient and strong winds.

q.s: The standard atmospheric pressure at sea level is:
q.x: Standard sea-level pressure is 1013.25 millibars.

q.s: India launched 'Operation Sagar Bandhu' to help Sri Lanka after Cyclone:
q.x: Operation Sagar Bandhu was India's relief mission after Cyclone Ditwah.

q.s: India's 'zero casualty' approach to cyclone management has been followed since Cyclone:
q.x: Phailin (2013) saw over a million people evacuated, setting the zero casualty model.

q.s: Tropical cyclones generally do not form within about 5 degrees of the Equator because:
o: The Coriolis force is too weak
q.x: Near the Equator the Coriolis force is too weak to set the air spinning.

q.s: In which layer of the atmosphere does temperature increase with height due to the absorption of ultraviolet radiation by ozone?
q.x: Ozone in the stratosphere absorbs UV and heats the layer, so temperature rises with height.

q.s: Ground-level ozone is a secondary pollutant formed in sunlight from:
o: Nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds
q.x: NOx and VOCs react in sunlight to form ground-level ozone, which is harmful unlike stratospheric ozone.

q.s: Pulicat Lake is separated from the Bay of Bengal by the island of:
q.x: Sriharikota separates Pulicat from the sea; Chilika is India's largest brackish-water lagoon and Pulicat the second.

q.s: Kolleru Lake lies between the deltas of which two rivers?
q.x: Kolleru, a freshwater lake, lies between the Godavari and Krishna deltas.

q.s: The Bhor Ghat in the Western Ghats provides a route between Mumbai and:
q.x: Bhor Ghat links Mumbai and Pune; Thal Ghat links Mumbai and Nashik.

q.s: Which of the following passes is NOT in the Western Ghats?
q.x: Nathu La is in Sikkim on the India-China border.

q.s: According to IMD, a 'rainy day' is a day on which the rainfall recorded in 24 hours is at least:
q.x: IMD counts a rainy day when 2.5 mm or more falls; a departure of -19% to +19% is 'normal'.

q.s: Agumbe, known as the 'Cherrapunji of the South', is located in:
q.x: Agumbe is in Shivamogga district of Karnataka.

q.s: The wettest place in India, Mawsynram, lies in which hills of Meghalaya?
q.x: Mawsynram is in the Khasi Hills, near Cherrapunji (Sohra).

q.s: The Rigvedic river 'Vitasta' is the present-day:
q.x: Vitasta is the Jhelum; Asikni is the Chenab, Vipasa the Beas and Shutudri the Sutlej.

q.s: The Rigvedic name of the river Sutlej was:
q.x: Shutudri is the Sutlej; Parushni is the Ravi.

q.s: The Annamayya dam that breached in the November 2021 floods is on the river:
q.x: The Annamayya dam is on the Cheyyeru, a Pennar tributary.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a tributary of the Pennar river?
q.x: Manjira is a tributary of the Godavari.

q.s: Which river basin in India has the highest level of water utilisation?
q.x: The Kaveri basin, mostly used for irrigation in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, has the highest utilisation.

q.s: In India's classification, a 'major' river basin is one with a catchment area of over:
q.x: Major basins exceed 20,000 sq km; India has 12 major and 8 composite basins.

q.s: Karewa soils of Kashmir are famous for the cultivation of:
q.x: Karewa soils are known for saffron; black soil is the cotton soil.

q.s: Which of the following crops is NOT typically grown on black soil?
q.x: Tea needs acidic, well-drained hill soils such as laterite; black soil suits cotton, jowar and soyabean.

q.s: The term 'edaphic factor' in ecology refers to:
q.x: Edaphic factors relate to soil; a pH of about 6-7 suits most crops.

q.s: Which of the following statements about soils is correct?
o: The saline soils of the Rayalaseema plateau are highly fertile
Arid soils have high moisture retention
A pH of about 6-7 is ideal for most common crops
q.x: Most crops do best at pH 6-7; edaphic means soil-related, arid soils hold little moisture and saline soils are unfit for cropping.

q.s: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched on 19 February 2015 at:
q.x: It was launched at Suratgarh, Rajasthan; since 2022-23 it runs under the RKVY.

q.s: Laterite soil is formed mainly by:
o: Intense leaching under high temperature and heavy rainfall
Weathering of basalt in dry conditions
q.x: Leaching removes silica and leaves iron and aluminium oxides; laterite is the most acidic of the major soils.

q.s: Which of the following crops is NOT generally grown on laterite soil?
q.x: With manure, laterite grows plantation crops like tea, coffee, rubber and cashew; wheat is grown on alluvial soils.

q.s: Which tree is known as the 'Flame of the forest'?
q.x: Palash (Butea monosperma) is the flame of the forest; Khejri is the 'king of the desert'.

q.s: The leaves of which tree are used as bidi wrappers?
q.x: Tendu leaves wrap bidis; Khair yields katha.

q.s: According to ISFR 2023, the total forest and tree cover of India is about what percentage of its geographical area?
q.x: Forest and tree cover together is about 25.17%; forest cover alone is about 21.76%.

q.s: Which of the following statements about forests (ISFR 2023) is correct?
o: Nearly all of the 1,445 sq km gain in green cover was true forest
India ranked 3rd in the world in forest-area gain during 2010-2020
Arunachal Pradesh has the largest forest area among States
Tree cover alone is about 25% of India's area
q.x: India was 3rd in forest-area gain; MP has the largest forest area, only about 156 sq km of the gain was forest, and forest plus tree cover is 25.17%.

q.s: As per the remeasurement reported in December 2024, India's coastline is:
q.x: The new figure is 11,098.81 km; the older figure was 7,516.6 km.

q.s: After the 2024 remeasurement, Andhra Pradesh's coastline ranks among the States:
q.x: Gujarat is first, Tamil Nadu second and Andhra Pradesh third with about 1,053 km.

q.s: The district worst affected in India by the tsunami of 26 December 2004 was:
q.x: Nagapattinam in Tamil Nadu suffered the most deaths; the tsunami came from the Mw 9.1 Sumatra-Andaman earthquake.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT hit by the Indian Ocean tsunami of 26 December 2004?
q.x: The tsunami struck the east and south coasts and the Andamans; Gujarat on the west coast was not affected.

q.s: In Indian land-use classification, land left uncultivated for more than five years is called:
q.x: Current fallow is up to one year, other fallow one to five years, and beyond five years it is culturable waste.

q.s: Which of the following statements about land-use classification in India is correct?
o: Culturable waste land is land left idle for less than one year
Current fallow is land left uncultivated for two to three years
Other fallow is land left uncultivated for more than five years
Punjab and Haryana have the highest share of net sown area
q.x: Punjab and Haryana have the highest NSA share; current fallow is up to a year, other fallow one to five years, and culturable waste over five years.

q.s: Bamboo drip irrigation is a traditional water system of:
q.x: Bamboo drip is from Meghalaya; kuhls are in Himachal and kuan or kui in Rajasthan.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of traditional water system and State is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Bamboo drip irrigation belongs to Meghalaya.

q.s: Malanjkhand, the leading copper mine of India, is in:
q.x: Malanjkhand (Balaghat) makes MP the top copper producer; Rajasthan has a near monopoly in lead-zinc.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a lead-zinc mine of Rajasthan?
q.x: Malanjkhand in Madhya Pradesh is a copper mine.

q.s: Mica is widely used in the electrical industry because it is:
q.x: Mica's insulating and heat-resistant properties suit electrical uses; the Koderma-Gaya-Hazaribagh belt is the largest.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a major mica-producing area of India?
q.x: Koderma (Jharkhand), Nellore (AP) and Bhilwara (Rajasthan) are mica belts; Singhbhum is known for iron ore and copper.

q.s: Inland fisheries account for about what share of India's total fish production?
q.x: Inland fisheries give over 75% of India's fish.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a cold-water fish?
q.x: Pomfret is a marine fish; cold-water fisheries above 1,500 m have trout and mahseer.

q.s: Which city is known as the 'Manchester of South India'?
q.x: Coimbatore is the Manchester of South India; Kanpur is the Manchester of the North and Ahmedabad the Manchester of India.

q.s: Which city is called the 'Pittsburgh of India'?
q.x: Jamshedpur, home of Tata Steel, is the Pittsburgh of India.

q.s: Asia's first Export Processing Zone was set up in 1965 at:
q.x: Kandla EPZ (1965) was Asia's first, though India's trade regime remained inward-looking till 1990.

q.s: India's first community radio station, Anna FM (2004), was set up by:
q.x: Anna FM was run by Anna University, Chennai, licensed by the Ministry of I&B.

q.s: Prasar Bharati, which runs All India Radio and Doordarshan, was set up under an Act of:
q.x: The Prasar Bharati Act was passed in 1990 and brought into force in 1997.

q.s: India's first World Heritage City, inscribed by UNESCO in 2017, is:
q.x: Ahmedabad became the first in 2017; Jaipur followed in 2019.

q.s: Gandikota, called the 'Grand Canyon of India', is located on the river Penna in which district?
q.x: Gandikota is in YSR Kadapa district.

q.s: Thimmamma Marrimanu, known for the largest banyan tree canopy, is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Thimmamma Marrimanu is in Sri Sathya Sai district; Talakona waterfall is in Tirupati district.

q.s: Orvakal in Andhra Pradesh is a node of which industrial corridor?
q.x: Orvakal (Kurnool) is on the Hyderabad-Bengaluru corridor; VCIC nodes include Visakhapatnam, Srikalahasti-Yerpedu and Kopparthy.

q.s: India's first coastal industrial corridor is the:
q.x: The VCIC is India's first coastal corridor and part of the East Coast Economic Corridor.

q.s: According to the 2011 Census, the least densely populated State of India was:
q.x: Arunachal Pradesh (17 per sq km) was the least dense; Delhi was the densest UT.

q.s: According to NFHS-5, the most widely used family planning method among married women in India is:
q.x: Female sterilisation is used by about 37.9% of married women.

q.s: Mission Parivar Vikas (2016) covers 146 high-fertility districts in how many States?
q.x: It covers 146 districts with TFR of 3 or more in 7 States.

q.s: The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) is conducted by the:
q.x: The PLFS is run by the NSO under MoSPI.
