q.s: The permanent campus of the Central Tribal University of Andhra Pradesh is in which district?
q.x: The campus is at Kondakarakam in Vizianagaram district; the university is listed in the 13th Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act.

q.s: The Chenchu tribe of Andhra Pradesh lives mainly in the:
q.x: Chenchus are a PVTG of the Nallamala around Srisailam; Yanadis live in the Nellore plains.

q.s: The settlements of the Sugali (Lambadi) tribe are called:
q.x: Lambadas live in thandas, mainly in Rayalaseema and central Andhra.

q.s: According to the 2011 Census, the district of Andhra Pradesh with the highest share of Scheduled Castes was:
q.x: Prakasam (23.19%) had the highest SC share; Visakhapatnam had the largest ST population.

q.s: According to the 2011 Census, Scheduled Castes formed about what share of Andhra Pradesh's population (13 districts)?
q.x: SCs numbered about 84.69 lakh, or 17.08%; STs were 5.53%.

q.s: A 'statutory town' in the Indian Census is a place that:
o: Has density of over 400 per sq km
Has a population of 5,000 or more
Has 75% male workers in non-farm work
Has a municipality, corporation, cantonment board or notified town area committee
q.x: Statutory towns are defined by law; the population, workforce and density tests define a census town.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the criteria for a 'census town' in India?
o: At least 75% of male main workers in non-farm work
Density of at least 400 persons per sq km
q.x: A census town meets the three demographic tests without a municipal body; a place with one is a statutory town. The 1981 criteria are retained for Census 2027.

q.s: Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0, aiming at 'Garbage Free' cities, was launched on:
q.x: SBM-U 2.0 was launched on 1 October 2021; the original SBM began on 2 October 2014.

q.s: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission is implemented by the:
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
q.x: The Rurban Mission develops rural clusters under the Ministry of Rural Development.

q.s: According to the 2011 Census, the most rural district of Andhra Pradesh (13-district map) was:
q.x: Srikakulam was only 16.16% urban; Visakhapatnam was the most urbanised.

q.s: The foundation stone of Amaravati, the capital of Andhra Pradesh, was laid by the Prime Minister on:
q.x: The foundation stone was laid on 22 October 2015 at Uddandarayunipalem; APCRDA had been set up on 30 December 2014.

q.s: The High Court of Andhra Pradesh began functioning in the Amaravati capital region on:
q.x: The separate AP High Court started at Amaravati on 1 January 2019.

q.s: Australian Aborigines and Melanesians belong to which racial group?
q.x: They are Australoid; the Inuit and East Asians are Mongoloid.

q.s: Which of the following peoples does NOT belong to the Mongoloid group?
q.x: Melanesians are Australoid.

q.s: The first Director of the Anthropological Survey of India was:
q.x: B.S. Guha headed AnSI, founded in 1945 at Varanasi and later based at Kolkata; Guha also gave a racial classification of Indians.

q.s: Which of the following is the oldest type of primary economic activity?
q.x: Hunting and gathering are the oldest; primary activities like farming are the most affected by climate.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a primary economic activity?
q.x: Manufacturing is a secondary activity.

q.s: The Great Barrier Reef, the largest coral reef system in the world, lies off the coast of:
q.x: It lies off Queensland in the Coral Sea; the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef is the next largest.

q.s: According to GCRMN 2026, major disturbances to coral reefs now come once every:
q.x: Disturbances now recur every 4-6 years, while recovery after a global bleaching takes over 15 years.

q.s: Which of the following protected areas is NOT a tiger reserve?
q.x: Gir is a lion sanctuary and national park; Melghat, Satpura and Simlipal are tiger reserves.

q.s: M-STrIPES, used in tiger reserves of India, is:
o: An app-based patrolling and monitoring system
q.x: M-STrIPES (Monitoring System for Tigers - Intensive Protection and Ecological Status) is an app-based patrolling tool.

q.s: The Sri Venkateswara Wildlife Sanctuary of Andhra Pradesh is associated with which hills?
q.x: SV Sanctuary covers the Seshachalam-Tirumala hills; the Penusila hills belong to the Sri Penusila Narasimha Sanctuary.

q.s: The boundary of a national park can be altered only on the recommendation of the:
q.x: Under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, NP boundaries change only on NBWL advice; grazing is not allowed in NPs.

q.s: The 'State of World Population' report is published by:
q.x: UNFPA publishes it; its 2025 edition was 'The Real Fertility Crisis'.

q.s: According to the UN World Urbanization Prospects 2025, the world's largest city is:
q.x: Jakarta is first and Dhaka second in the 2025 edition, which uses a new city definition.

q.s: The term 'Green Revolution' was coined in 1968 by:
q.x: USAID's William Gaud coined the term; Borlaug developed the high-yielding wheat.

q.s: CIMMYT, the international maize and wheat research centre, is located in:
q.x: CIMMYT is in Mexico; IRRI, which released IR8, is at Los Banos in the Philippines.

q.s: The Indian-origin mathematician who won the Fields Medal in 2014 is:
q.x: Manjul Bhargava won in 2014; Akshay Venkatesh won in 2018.

q.s: The first Asian to win the Turing Award (1994) was:
q.x: Raj Reddy won the Turing Award in 1994 for work in artificial intelligence.

q.s: The AI4AP Police Project of Andhra Pradesh (2026) is mainly meant for:
o: Traffic management, crime prediction and investigation
q.x: AI4AP is for policing; the Microsoft-ICRISAT sowing app was piloted in Kurnool in 2016.

q.s: Which consensus mechanism of blockchains consumes the most energy?
q.x: In Proof of Work miners race to solve puzzles, using huge computing power; Proof of Stake picks validators by staked coins.

q.s: IN-SPACe, the single-window agency for private space activities, is headquartered at:
q.x: IN-SPACe (2020) under the Department of Space is at Ahmedabad, chaired by Pawan Kumar Goenka.

q.s: Vikram-S, India's first privately built rocket launched under Mission Prarambh (2022), was developed by:
q.x: Skyroot Aerospace of Hyderabad built Vikram-S, which reached 89.5 km.

q.s: Under the Indian Space Policy 2023, the commercialisation of mature ISRO technologies is the role of:
q.x: NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) commercialises mature technology; IN-SPACe authorises non-governmental entities.

q.s: Under the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture, Soil Health Cards are issued to farmers:
q.x: Soil Health Cards are issued free every two years; since 2022-23 NMSA runs under PM-RKVY.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the eight National Missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change?
o: National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency
q.x: Namami Gange/NMCG is not an NAPCC mission; the eight include Solar, Energy Efficiency, Water, Sustainable Habitat, Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture and Strategic Knowledge.

q.s: 'Vyommitra', developed by ISRO, is:
o: A half-humanoid robot for the uncrewed Gaganyaan flight
q.x: Vyommitra is a half-humanoid robot; Daksh is DRDO's bomb-disposal robot.

q.s: The first Made-in-India surgical robotic system is:
q.x: SSI Mantra by SS Innovations is the first indigenous surgical robot.

q.s: The SSLV Launch Complex at Kulasekarapattinam is located in which district of Tamil Nadu?
q.x: Kulasekarapattinam is in Thoothukudi district.

q.s: The 100th launch from Sriharikota took place on 29 January 2025 with:
q.x: GSLV-F15 carried the NavIC satellite NVS-02 as the 100th launch from Sriharikota.

q.s: Thumba near Thiruvananthapuram was chosen as India's first rocket launching station because:
o: It is close to the Tropic of Cancer
The geomagnetic equator passes through it
q.x: Thumba lies on the magnetic equator, ideal for upper-atmosphere studies with sounding rockets.

q.s: PSLV-C37, which carried a Cartosat-2 series satellite in 2017, set a record by launching how many satellites in one mission?
q.x: PSLV-C37 placed 104 satellites in orbit.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an Earth observation satellite series of ISRO?
q.x: NavIC is India's regional navigation satellite system.

q.s: ANUSAT, the first student satellite launched by ISRO (2009), was built by:
q.x: Anna University built ANUSAT; IIT Kanpur built Jugnu.

q.s: NISAR, launched by GSLV-F16 in July 2025, is a joint Earth observation mission of ISRO and:
q.x: NISAR (NASA-ISRO SAR) is with NASA; INSAT-3DS was funded by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's City Flood Alert system, first implemented in Vijayawada, was developed with:
q.x: RTGS and APSDMA built it with IIT Gandhinagar.

q.s: Which instrument on Chandrayaan-3's Pragyan rover confirmed the presence of sulphur on the lunar surface in situ?
q.x: LIBS (Laser Induced Breakdown Spectroscope) confirmed sulphur; the APXS found soil rich in iron and magnesium.

q.s: 'Mission Shakti' (2019) of India refers to:
o: A women's safety scheme of DRDO
q.x: Mission Shakti was the 2019 ASAT test; Operation Shakti was Pokhran-II (1998) and Smiling Buddha Pokhran-I (1974).

q.s: PRAGATI, the ICT platform for monitoring projects and grievances launched in 2015, is run by the:
q.x: PRAGATI is chaired by the PM through the PMO; SARATHI and VAHAN belong to MoRTH.

q.s: India's oldest nuclear power units at Tarapur (units 1 and 2) are of which reactor type?
q.x: Tarapur 1-2 are BWRs; Kudankulam has Russian VVERs and the PFBR at Kalpakkam is a fast breeder.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a nuclear power station in India?
q.x: Ramagundam has a coal-based thermal plant.

q.s: Under the Nuclear Energy Mission, India's target for nuclear power capacity by 2047 is:
q.x: The 2047 target is 100 GW; 22.38 GW is the 2031-32 target.

q.s: The SHANTI Act, 2025 repealed the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010 and the:
q.x: It repealed the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the CLND Act, 2010.

q.s: About 26 million households were given electricity connections under the scheme:
q.x: Saubhagya (2017) connected about 26 million households; DDUGJY strengthened rural feeders.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India's energy use is correct?
o: Industry uses about 50% of India's electricity
Cooking energy demand is projected to rise sharply by 2040
Agriculture is projected to be the largest energy consumer by 2040
q.x: Industry uses about half the electricity and will remain the largest consumer; cooking demand is projected to fall and the 26 million connections came under Saubhagya.

q.s: India aims to raise the share of natural gas in its primary energy mix to what level by 2030?
q.x: The target is 15% by 2030; about half of India's gas is imported.

q.s: The 'One Nation One Gas Grid' initiative is under the:
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
q.x: The gas grid comes under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

q.s: In petroleum geology, the organic-rich shale in which oil is formed is called the:
q.x: Oil forms in the source rock, collects in porous reservoir rock and is sealed by impervious cap rock.

q.s: In July 2017, the clean energy cess that funded the National Clean Energy Fund was merged into the:
q.x: The clean environment cess was subsumed into the GST Compensation Cess.

q.s: The National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE) is located at:
q.x: NIWE is at Chennai; NISE is at Gurugram and NIBE at Kapurthala.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an institution under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy?
q.x: NTPC is a power PSU under the Ministry of Power.

q.s: India's installed wind power capacity crossed 50 GW in:
q.x: Wind crossed 50 GW in March 2025; renewables gave about 22% of generation in 2024-25.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India's electricity in 2024-25 is correct?
o: Coal gave less than half of electricity generation
Renewables gave about 22% of electricity generation
Wind capacity crossed 50 GW in March 2023
Solar overtook coal in total generation
q.x: Renewables gave about 22% while coal still gave about 69-75%; wind crossed 50 GW in March 2025.

q.s: Under the 2024 Viability Gap Funding scheme for offshore wind, the first 1 GW is to be set up off the coasts of:
q.x: The first 1 GW is split 500 MW off Gujarat and 500 MW off Tamil Nadu; the 2015 policy allows wind farms in the EEZ.

q.s: The largest biogeographic zone of India, in which Andhra Pradesh lies, is the:
q.x: The Deccan Peninsula is the largest zone; the Trans-Himalaya covers about 5.7%.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the ten biogeographic zones of India?
q.x: The zones include Trans-Himalaya, Himalaya, Desert, Semi-Arid, Western Ghats, Deccan Peninsula, Gangetic Plain, Coasts, North-East and Islands.

q.s: The only viable population of the Hangul (Kashmir stag) is found in:
q.x: The Hangul survives in Dachigam NP near Srinagar.

q.s: The Great Indian Hornbill is the state bird of Kerala and:
q.x: It is the state bird of both Arunachal Pradesh and Kerala.

q.s: The mascot 'Gibi' of CMS COP13 (Gandhinagar, 2020) represented the:
q.x: Gibi was the Great Indian Bustard, a critically endangered bird of Gujarat and Rajasthan.

q.s: Vanamahotsav, observed in the first week of July, was started in 1950 by:
q.x: K.M. Munshi, then Union Agriculture Minister, began Vanamahotsav.

q.s: The term 'social forestry' was first used in India in 1976 by the:
q.x: The National Commission on Agriculture (1976) used the term.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a natural source of air pollution?
q.x: Vehicle exhaust is anthropogenic; fires, volcanoes, dust storms and pollen are natural sources.

q.s: Carbon monoxide is dangerous to humans mainly because it:
o: Combines with haemoglobin far more readily than oxygen
q.x: CO's affinity for haemoglobin is about 200-250 times that of oxygen, forming carboxyhaemoglobin.

q.s: The National Lake Conservation Plan (NLCP) was launched in:
q.x: NLCP began in 2001 and was merged with the wetlands programme as NPCA in 2013.

q.s: The National River Conservation Plan, which broadened the Ganga Action Plan, was launched in:
q.x: NRCP began in 1995; the Yamuna Action Plan in 1993.

q.s: An Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is carried out:
o: Every five years for all industries
q.x: EIA evaluates a project before it begins; an environmental audit checks an operating unit.

q.s: The western zonal bench of the National Green Tribunal sits at:
q.x: The NGT sits at Delhi (principal), Pune, Bhopal, Chennai and Kolkata; Jodhpur and Shillong are circuit benches.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a regular place of sitting of the National Green Tribunal?
q.x: Jodhpur is only a circuit bench; the NGT sits at Delhi, Pune, Bhopal, Chennai and Kolkata.

q.s: COP30 of the UNFCCC, the first COP held in the Amazon, took place at:
q.x: COP30 was at Belem, Brazil; COP28 was at Dubai.

q.s: COP31 of the UNFCCC in 2026 is hosted at:
q.x: COP31 is hosted at Antalya, Turkiye.

q.s: The definitive phase of the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) began on:
q.x: The transitional phase began in October 2023 and the definitive phase on 1 January 2026.

q.s: Which of the following sectors is NOT covered by the EU's CBAM?
q.x: CBAM covers iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity.

q.s: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium and is transmitted by the:
q.x: The female Anopheles carries Plasmodium; Aedes spreads dengue and Culex filaria.

q.s: Relapsing malaria due to dormant liver stages (hypnozoites) is caused by:
q.x: P. vivax (and P. ovale) form hypnozoites; in humans parasites multiply first in the liver, then in red blood cells.

q.s: The 'Your Capital, Your Right' campaign on unclaimed financial assets (2025) is led by the:
q.x: It is led by the Department of Financial Services, with the RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA and IEPFA as partners.

q.s: The India-China Special Representatives mechanism on the boundary question was set up in:
q.x: It was set up in 2003; the 25th round was held at Beijing between Ajit Doval and Wang Yi.

q.s: The AI Action Summit of February 2025 was held in:
q.x: The AI Action Summit was at Paris in 2025; India hosted the AI Impact Summit in 2026.

q.s: India Energy Week 2026 was held at:
q.x: India Energy Week 2026 was held in Goa; the World Governments Summit is held at Dubai.

q.s: India launched the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) at the East Asia Summit held in 2019 at:
q.x: IPOI was launched at Bangkok in 2019; it is a voluntary, non-treaty initiative with seven pillars.

q.s: The Third UN Ocean Conference (June 2025) at Nice was co-hosted by France and:
q.x: France and Costa Rica co-hosted UNOC3; its outcome supports SDG 14 (Life below water).

q.s: Since 1861, United States currency notes have been signed by:
o: The Treasurer and the Secretary of the Treasury
q.x: Only the Treasurer and Treasury Secretary have signed US notes, so a sitting President's signature in 2026 is a first.

q.s: The International Solar Alliance (ISA), launched by India and France at COP21 in 2015, is headquartered at:
q.x: The ISA is headquartered at Gurugram, Haryana.

q.s: Under the India-New Zealand FTA, India will remove or reduce tariffs on about what share of imports from New Zealand?
q.x: India will cut tariffs on about 95% of NZ imports, and New Zealand is to facilitate about $20 billion of investment in India.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four non-EU members of the Schengen area?
q.x: Romania is an EU member (full Schengen member from 2025); the non-EU four are Iceland, Norway, Switzerland and Liechtenstein.

q.s: India's most recent (eighth) term as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council was in:
q.x: India's eighth term was 2021-22; its seventh was 2011-12.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a permanent member of the UN Security Council?
q.x: The five permanent members are the USA, UK, France, Russia and China.

q.s: Bulgaria joined the European Union in 2007 along with:
q.x: Bulgaria and Romania joined in 2007; Croatia joined in 2013. Bulgaria became the 21st euro country.

q.s: Under the Maastricht criteria for adopting the euro, government debt must be below:
q.x: Debt must be below 60% and the deficit below 3% of GDP.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an official language of Belgium?
q.x: Belgium's official languages are Dutch, French and German.

q.s: The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the:
q.x: Hormuz links the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman; about 90% of India's LPG imports pass through it.

q.s: India approached the IMF for assistance after the oil shock of:
q.x: The 1979 shock (oil from about $13 to $34 a barrel) caused a BoP crisis and India took an IMF loan in 1981.

q.s: Chabahar port, developed with Indian help, lies on the:
q.x: Chabahar is on the Gulf of Oman, outside the Persian Gulf, and is Iran's only oceanic port.

q.s: The International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) connects India with:
o: Iran, Russia, Central Asia and Europe
q.x: The 7,200-km INSTC links India, Iran, Russia, Central Asia and Europe.

q.s: The India Semiconductor Mission was set up in 2021 under the:
q.x: ISM was set up under MeitY; Semicon 2.0 was notified in August 2026.

q.s: Chandrayaan-4, targeted for 2028, is planned as a:
q.x: Chandrayaan-4 aims to bring back samples from the Moon.

q.s: CERVAVAC, India's first indigenous quadrivalent HPV vaccine against cervical cancer, was developed by:
q.x: CERVAVAC is made by the Serum Institute and covers HPV types 6, 11, 16 and 18.

q.s: Under WHO's 90-70-90 targets for cervical cancer elimination, 90% of girls are to be fully vaccinated against HPV by the age of:
q.x: 90% of girls vaccinated by 15, 70% of women screened, and 90% of those with disease treated.

q.s: The Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces of India is the:
q.x: The President is the Supreme Commander under Article 53(2).

q.s: The intense heating of a space capsule during re-entry into the atmosphere is mainly caused by:
o: Compression of the air in front of the capsule
q.x: Re-entry heat comes mainly from compressing the air ahead of the capsule (shock heating), not friction.

q.s: IBM's planned fault-tolerant quantum computer (2029) is based on which type of qubits?
q.x: IBM uses superconducting qubits; trapped ions are used by firms like IonQ.

q.s: In satellite navigation security, transmitting false signals to mislead a receiver is called:
q.x: Spoofing sends false signals; jamming blocks signals.

q.s: Under the Outer Space Treaty of 1967, responsibility for national space activities, including those of private entities, rests with:
q.x: Article VI makes States responsible for all national space activities, governmental or private.

q.s: The James Webb Space Telescope was launched in:
q.x: JWST was launched on 25 December 2021.

q.s: The KA-SAT cyberattack of 2022, at the start of the Russia-Ukraine war, hit the satellite network of:
q.x: The attack disabled modems on Viasat's KA-SAT network.

q.s: The Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS) was established in 2008 with its first chair being:
q.x: India launched IONS in 2008 and was its first chair; India chairs it again for 2025-27.

q.s: Qeshm Island, in the news for an oil spill in 2026, belongs to:
q.x: Qeshm is an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz.

q.s: Uttarakhand's first real-time glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) early warning system is at Vasundhara Lake in which district?
q.x: It is at Vasundhara Lake in Chamoli; the National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme covers four Himalayan States.

q.s: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 was enacted by Parliament under which Article of the Constitution?
q.x: Article 253 lets Parliament implement international agreements; the Act followed the Stockholm Declaration of 1972.

q.s: Which of the following Articles does NOT relate to protection of the environment?
q.x: Article 280 deals with the Finance Commission; Article 21 has been read to include the right to a healthy environment.

q.s: Under its updated NDC (2022), India aims to reduce the emissions intensity of its GDP from 2005 levels by 2030 by:
q.x: The target is 45%; India has set net zero for 2070, while China aims at 2060.

q.s: India's target year for achieving net-zero emissions is:
q.x: India announced net zero by 2070 at COP26 (Glasgow).

q.s: According to the WHO, household air pollution causes about how many deaths in the world every year?
q.x: About 3.2 million deaths a year, mostly from ischaemic heart disease; total air pollution causes about 7 million.

q.s: Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary is located in:
q.x: Kumbhalgarh (1971) is in Rajasthan's Aravallis; the Parvati-Arga Bird Sanctuary is in Uttar Pradesh.

q.s: Tso Kar, a high-altitude Ramsar site, is located in:
q.x: Tso Kar is in Ladakh; Kole Wetlands (Kerala) are known for below-sea-level rice farming.

q.s: Bhitarkanika, whose mangroves reduced damage from Cyclone Dana, is in:
q.x: Bhitarkanika is a mangrove national park and Ramsar site in Odisha.

q.s: India's first two cities accredited as Wetland Cities under the Ramsar Convention (January 2025) were:
q.x: Indore and Udaipur were accredited; MISHTI aims to restore 540 sq km of mangroves.

q.s: The Global Gender Gap Index is published by the:
q.x: The WEF publishes it; UNDP brings out the Gender Inequality Index in the HDR.

q.s: Which of the following indices is NOT published by UNDP?
q.x: The Global Gender Gap Index is published by the World Economic Forum.

q.s: According to the 2011 Census, which State ranked second in population after Uttar Pradesh?
q.x: Maharashtra was second; Bihar third, West Bengal fourth and undivided Andhra Pradesh fifth.

q.s: Designation of individuals as terrorists in India was made possible by the 2019 amendment to the:
q.x: The UAPA Amendment, 2019 allowed individuals to be designated; a 'terrorist act' is defined in Section 15 of the UAPA.

q.s: Which State is the largest producer of wool in India?
q.x: Rajasthan produces about 47.5% of India's wool.

q.s: As of December 2025, the State with the highest installed renewable energy capacity in India was:
q.x: Gujarat led with about 42.58 GW; Rajasthan is close behind.

q.s: The Responsible Nations Index 2026 was brought out by:
q.x: Its first edition was by the World Intellectual Foundation, New Delhi, and was launched by former President Ram Nath Kovind.

q.s: In Swachh Survekshan 2024-25, the Super Swachh League was topped by:
q.x: Indore topped the Super Swachh League; Ahmedabad was the cleanest big city outside it.

q.s: The first Indian to receive the Oskar Klein Medal (2026), for work in theoretical physics, is:
q.x: String theorist Ashoke Sen of ICTS received the Oskar Klein Medal.

q.s: The 'Order of Zayed' is a high civilian honour of:
q.x: The Order of Zayed is a UAE honour named after Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan.

q.s: A single Nobel Prize can be shared by at most:
q.x: The statutes allow at most three laureates per prize (organisations can share the Peace Prize).

q.s: The first Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences (1969) was awarded to:
q.x: Frisch and Tinbergen shared the first economics prize in 1969.

q.s: The COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal is awarded jointly by COSPAR and ISRO:
q.x: It is given every two years at the COSPAR Scientific Assembly; Annapurni Subramaniam received it in 2026.

q.s: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2025 was awarded for the development of:
q.x: The 2025 Chemistry prize went for metal-organic frameworks; the Physics prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling.

q.s: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2025 was awarded for discoveries concerning:
q.x: It recognised peripheral immune tolerance (regulatory T cells).

q.s: László Krasznahorkai, Nobel laureate in Literature 2025, is from:
q.x: He is the second Hungarian laureate after Imre Kertesz (2002); his novel Satantango was filmed by Bela Tarr.

q.s: The Sahitya Akademi functions under the:
q.x: It is under the Ministry of Culture; it was inaugurated in March 1954 and first gave awards in 1955.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three national academies set up in the 1950s?
q.x: The National Book Trust (1957) is a publishing body under the Ministry of Education, not an academy.

q.s: Which of the following is the oldest of India's National Sports Awards?
q.x: The Arjuna Award dates from 1961; Khel Ratna began in 1991-92 and Dronacharya in 1985.

q.s: India's National Sports Awards are normally presented on National Sports Day, which is observed on:
q.x: 29 August is the birthday of Major Dhyan Chand.

q.s: The first Asian Games, held at New Delhi in 1951, were opened by:
q.x: President Rajendra Prasad opened the Games in March 1951.

q.s: R. Praggnanandhaa became the first Indian to win the Grand Chess Tour by beating in the Finals at St. Louis:
q.x: He beat Fabiano Caruana; he had earlier become the first Indian to win Norway Chess.

q.s: The Olympic Council of Asia is headquartered in:
q.x: The OCA (1982) is based in Kuwait City; Doha hosts the 2030 and Riyadh the 2034 Asian Games.

q.s: Which cities will host the 2030 and 2034 Asian Games respectively?
q.x: Doha will host 2030 and Riyadh 2034; India hosted in 1951 and 1982.

q.s: The India Open badminton tournament held at New Delhi is a BWF event of which level?
q.x: The India Open is a Super 750 event.

q.s: In the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026, Bangladesh was replaced by:
q.x: Scotland replaced Bangladesh, who refused to play in India.

q.s: The SAI National Centre of Excellence that serves as the Nodal Centre for Para Sports is at:
q.x: SAI NCoE Gandhinagar is the nodal centre; Gujarat's Para High Performance Centre is also at Gandhinagar.

q.s: Telugu was declared a classical language of India in:
q.x: Telugu and Kannada were declared classical in 2008; Tamil was the first in 2004.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a classical language of India?
q.x: Urdu is not a classical language; Marathi was added in 2024, bringing the total to 11.

q.s: 'Vande Mataram' was included in the novel Anandamath, written by:
q.x: Bankim Chandra wrote Anandamath (1882); the song first appeared in Bangadarshan in 1875.

q.s: Vande Mataram was adopted as the National Song of India on:
q.x: The Constituent Assembly adopted it on 24 January 1950, along with the National Anthem.

q.s: The Vice-President of India in 2026, who released the book 'Advantage India', is:
q.x: C.P. Radhakrishnan became Vice-President in 2025.

q.s: The internationally recognised symbol of Breast Cancer Awareness Month (October) is the:
q.x: The pink ribbon is its symbol, hence 'Pink October'; the red ribbon stands for HIV/AIDS awareness.

q.s: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas, observed on 9 January, marks:
o: Gandhi's return from South Africa in 1915
Gandhi's departure for South Africa in 1893
The founding of the Indian Diaspora Ministry
q.x: Gandhi returned to India from South Africa on 9 January 1915.

q.s: The Bihar Museum, Patna, was designed by the Japanese architect:
q.x: Fumihiko Maki's firm designed the Bihar Museum.

q.s: The 21st East Asia Summit in 2026 was held at:
q.x: The Philippines chaired ASEAN in 2026, so the EAS was held at Manila.

q.s: Earth's Rotation Day (8 January) recalls Leon Foucault's pendulum demonstration of 1851, made at the:
q.x: Foucault's famous demonstration was at the Pantheon; the Eiffel Tower was built only in 1889.

q.s: National Siddha Day (6 January) marks the birth anniversary of:
q.x: Siddha Day honours Sage Agastya, regarded as the father of Siddha medicine; Ayurveda Day honours Dhanvantari.

q.s: The 300th birth anniversary of which ruler was marked on 31 May 2025?
q.x: Ahilyabai Holkar was born on 31 May 1725; Bhupen Hazarika's birth centenary was also marked in 2025.

q.s: The President of the 81st UN General Assembly, Khalilur Rahman, is from:
q.x: Khalilur Rahman, Bangladesh's Foreign Minister, succeeds Annalena Baerbock and defeated Andreas Kakouris of Cyprus.

q.s: Kami Rita Sherpa, record holder for the most Everest ascents, made his 32nd ascent in May 2026. He is from:
q.x: Kami Rita is a Nepali Sherpa; Lhakpa Sherpa holds the women's record of 11 ascents.

q.s: Barham Salih, who became UN High Commissioner for Refugees from 1 January 2026, is a former President of:
q.x: Barham Salih of Iraq succeeded Filippo Grandi at UNHCR.

q.s: Shaikha Al Nowais, the first woman to lead UN Tourism, is from:
q.x: She is from the UAE.

q.s: In the Forbes World's Billionaires list of April 2025, India ranked third in the number of billionaires after:
q.x: India, with 205 billionaires, was third after the USA and China; Mukesh Ambani was the richest Indian.

q.s: According to the SRS Statistical Report 2024, the State with the highest Total Fertility Rate was:
q.x: Bihar had the highest TFR (2.9) and Delhi the lowest (1.2).

q.s: The headquarters of the North Eastern Council is at:
q.x: The NEC (1972) is at Shillong.

q.s: Which of the following cities is NOT the headquarters of a Zonal Council?
q.x: The Southern Zonal Council is at Chennai; Northern is at New Delhi, Eastern at Kolkata and Western at Mumbai.

q.s: The Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) guards India's borders with:
q.x: SSB guards the Nepal and Bhutan borders; ITBP guards the China border and Assam Rifles the Myanmar border.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Central Armed Police Force?
q.x: The Coast Guard is an armed force under the Ministry of Defence; CAPFs are under the Home Ministry.

q.s: The headquarters of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) is at:
q.x: ICAO is at Montreal, Canada.

q.s: In India, aviation security is the responsibility of the:
q.x: BCAS is the aviation security regulator; the DGCA regulates safety.

q.s: NAFIS, used in criminal investigation in India, is a national database of:
q.x: NAFIS is the National Automated Fingerprint Identification System; e-Sakshya handles digital evidence.

q.s: Under the Women's Reservation Act, 2023, the quota of seats reserved for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies is:
q.x: One-third of seats will be reserved, after the next Census and delimitation.

q.s: In 2025-26, the Supreme Court held that safe travel on highways is part of the right guaranteed under:
q.x: The Court treated safe highway travel as part of the right to life under Article 21.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court permit passive euthanasia in India for the first time (2011)?
q.x: Aruna Shanbaug (2011) allowed passive euthanasia; Common Cause (2018) recognised living wills.

q.s: Living wills (advance medical directives) were recognised by the Supreme Court in:
q.x: Common Cause v. Union of India (2018) recognised living wills and the right to die with dignity.

q.s: The Supreme Court's opinion of November 2025 on the Presidential Reference about Governors' assent to Bills was given by a Bench led by:
q.x: A five-judge Bench led by CJI B.R. Gavai rejected deemed assent and court-imposed timelines, but allowed a limited mandamus.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The IBC, 2016 received assent in May 2016
The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026 replaced a GST Ordinance
A Registered Unrecognised Political Party gets a reserved symbol
q.x: The IBC got assent in May 2016 and the IBBI has 10 members; RUPPs get only free symbols.

q.s: Which of the following statements about GST growth in the southern States in 2026 is NOT correct?
o: Telangana recorded the highest southern growth in September (18%)
Andhra Pradesh recorded 11% growth in September
Andhra Pradesh recorded the highest southern growth in October (24%)
q.x: Andhra Pradesh grew only 6% in September 2026; 11% was Kerala's growth.

q.s: In the GST Council, the vote of the Central Government carries a weightage of:
q.x: The Centre has one-third and the States two-thirds; decisions need three-fourths of weighted votes, so no decision can pass without the Centre.

q.s: The Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP) is administered by:
q.x: GIC Re administers the pool; New India Assurance issued its first policy.

q.s: Which are the world's only two doubly landlocked countries?
q.x: Uzbekistan and Liechtenstein are doubly landlocked; Uzbekistan became the 11th country to accept UPI.

q.s: The first country to accept India's UPI payments was:
q.x: Bhutan was the first; Uzbekistan became the 11th.

q.s: The National Bamboo Mission is implemented by the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
q.x: It is under the Ministry of Agriculture; the 2017 amendment of the Indian Forest Act removed bamboo grown on non-forest land from the definition of 'tree'.

q.s: Which State produces about three-fourths of India's makhana (fox nut)?
q.x: Bihar dominates makhana output; the National Makhana Board was set up there in 2025.

q.s: In the piped natural gas supply chain, imported LNG is first converted back to gas at:
q.x: LNG is regasified at coastal terminals, carried by trunk pipelines to City Gate Stations and then to homes.

q.s: Interest rates on small savings schemes in India are revised every quarter by the:
q.x: The Ministry of Finance sets them; collections go to the National Small Savings Fund in the Public Account.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a small savings scheme?
q.x: APY is a pension scheme run by PFRDA; it is not part of the National Small Savings Fund schemes.

q.s: National Education Day, observed on 11 November, marks the birth anniversary of:
q.x: 11 November is Maulana Azad's birth anniversary; the Vidya Vahini portal was launched that day. Teachers' Day (5 September) honours Radhakrishnan.

q.s: Under the Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana, the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) has been renamed:
q.x: IGNOAPS became the PM Vriddhavastha Pension Yojana; NFBS became the PM Parivar Labh Yojana.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the National Social Assistance Programme?
q.x: PM-KISAN is an income support scheme for farmers under the Ministry of Agriculture.

q.s: The Rashtriya Gokul Mission, for the conservation of indigenous bovine breeds, was launched in:
q.x: It was launched in December 2014; the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre at Bhildi (Banaskantha) was set up under it.

q.s: The headquarters of the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) is at:
q.x: NDDB is at Anand, Gujarat.

q.s: The National Green Hydrogen Mission (2023) has an outlay of:
q.x: NGHM has Rs 19,744 crore; UJALA has distributed about 37 crore LED bulbs.

q.s: India's Universal Immunisation Programme was launched in:
q.x: UIP began in 1985; WHO's Expanded Programme on Immunization dates from 1974 and Mission Indradhanush from 2014.

q.s: Mission Indradhanush, launched in 2014, is a programme of:
q.x: It is a Government of India drive to cover unvaccinated and partially vaccinated children.

q.s: The Startup India initiative was launched on:
q.x: Startup India began on 16 January 2016 (National Startup Day); Gati Shakti came on 13 October 2021.

q.s: The Narco Coordination Centre (NCORD) mechanism functions under the:
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
q.x: NCORD is a four-tier mechanism of the MHA; the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan is run by the Ministry of Social Justice.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to prohibit intoxicating drinks and drugs except for medicinal purposes?
q.x: Article 47 deals with nutrition, public health and prohibition.

q.s: Under Section 23 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, a transfer of property by a senior citizen can be:
o: Declared void if the transferee fails to maintain them
q.x: Section 23 lets a tribunal void a transfer made on condition of maintenance if the transferee fails to provide it.

q.s: From January 2025, the PLFS gives monthly labour estimates on the basis of the:
q.x: Monthly bulletins use the Current Weekly Status; July 2026 unemployment was 5.1%.

q.s: Section 66A of the Information Technology Act was struck down by the Supreme Court in:
q.x: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015) struck down Section 66A as violating free speech.

q.s: Section 196 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (formerly IPC 153A) deals with:
q.x: BNS 196 covers promoting enmity; BNS 299 (ex-295A) covers insulting religion.

q.s: Guidelines to prevent mob lynching were issued by the Supreme Court in the case of:
q.x: Tehseen Poonawalla (2018) laid down mob lynching guidelines; the Bezbaruah Committee (2014) dealt with racial discrimination against people from the North East.

q.s: Under the PM-RAHAT scheme for road accident victims, cashless treatment is provided up to:
q.x: PM-RAHAT gives up to Rs 1.5 lakh per victim for 7 days; a Rah-Veer gets Rs 25,000.

q.s: India's 100th Ramsar site, Surha Tal, announced on 5 June 2026, is in:
q.x: Surha Tal is an oxbow lake of the Ganga in Ballia, UP, the State's 13th Ramsar site.

q.s: The Gulf of Mannar Marine Biosphere Reserve became a Ramsar site in:
q.x: It was designated in 2022; Longwood Shola was designated in 2024.

q.s: Which of the following Ramsar sites is NOT in Tamil Nadu?
o: Gulf of Mannar Marine Biosphere Reserve
q.x: Kolleru is in Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: The Bhoj Wetlands of Bhopal were designated a Ramsar site in:
q.x: Bhoj Wetlands and Tsomoriri were designated in 2002; Tawa Reservoir in 2024.

q.s: Which of the following Ramsar sites is NOT in Madhya Pradesh?
q.x: Tsomoriri is in Ladakh.

q.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's Sanjeevani tribal strategy, the 'Adivathalli Bata' initiative concerns:
q.x: Adivathalli Bata builds about 900 km of roads to tribal habitations.

q.s: From 1 October 2026, the Central share of NSAP pensions in Andhra Pradesh is credited through:
q.x: The Central share now goes to Aadhaar-linked bank accounts via SNA-SPARSH.

q.s: The permanent Pan-IIT Council at Amaravati is being set up in partnership with:
q.x: It is with PanIIT Alumni India and includes a Rs 500-crore venture fund and a mentor network.

q.s: The International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking is observed on:
q.x: 26 June is the anti-drug day; 31 May is World No Tobacco Day and 1 December World AIDS Day.

q.s: Which of the following is the first of the 'Padi Sutralu' (ten principles) of Swarna Andhra @2047?
q.x: Zero Poverty is the first principle; the 'Drone Capital of India' goal falls under Deep Tech.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's Building Penalisation Scheme (BPS) 2025 regularises unauthorised constructions made up to:
q.x: It covers constructions from 1 January 1985 to 31 August 2025; the APCRDA Capital City Area is excluded.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's separate Agriculture Budget for 2026-27 was presented by:
q.x: Agriculture Minister K. Atchannaidu presented it; it is part of the Rs 3.32 lakh crore State budget.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's GSDP target for 2025-26, set in September 2025, is:
q.x: The target is Rs 18.65 lakh crore; the 25% growth target is for tourism.

q.s: According to the 2011 Census, the literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh (13 districts) was about:
q.x: AP's literacy was 67.35%, below the national 72.98% (74.04% is India's overall figure).

q.s: Which of the following statements comparing Andhra Pradesh with India is correct?
o: AP's IMR (SRS 2024) is higher than India's
AP's literacy is above the national average
AP's multidimensional poverty (2019-21) is lower than India's
AP's literacy and IMR both exceed national figures
q.x: AP's MPI poverty is 6.06% against India's 14.96%; its IMR is 18 against 24, but literacy is below the national average.

q.s: The Swarna Naravaripalli rooftop solarisation project in Tirupati district received the SKOCH Award for implementing:
q.x: It was for PM Surya Ghar; grid integration was done by APSPDCL.

q.s: The Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar 2025 was given to the:
q.x: It went to the Army Paralympic Node, Pune; no Khel Ratna was given for 2025.

q.s: The Godavari Pushkarams are held once every:
q.x: Pushkarams of a river come once in 12 years, when Jupiter enters the river's zodiac sign; the next Godavari Pushkaram is in 2027.

q.s: The power of High Courts to issue writs for Fundamental Rights and other legal rights is given in:
q.x: Article 226 is wider than Article 32, covering other legal rights too.

q.s: Which Article declares every High Court to be a Court of Record?
q.x: Article 215 makes the High Court a court of record; Article 129 does so for the Supreme Court.
